commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Recipe] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: MI355X PD, DBO / SP prefill, Quark MXFP4, mono decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

AMD MI355X additions to the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipe (`recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml` only). No other open PR changes this recipe.

## Claims

1. **PD on MI355X**: `pd_cluster` renders the guide's 1P1D. One TP4 engine per role; BLHNC KV layout and NIXL with 4 threads; the prefill node drops `indexer_decode_cp` and offloads KV to host memory in 1 GiB HugeTLB pages (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`).
2. **TP4 on MI355X** for `single_node_tp` (Hopper keeps the FP8 variant's TP8).
3. **DBO / SP prefill** (opt-in feature, MI355X single node): SP + DBO, DBO, or SP. Guide section with the flags; one 32K-token prefill takes 1035 ms plain, 655 ms with DBO, 484 ms with SP + DBO (MXFP8 MoE).
4. **MXFP4 (Quark) variant**: `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, MXFP4 W4A4 experts on the AITER MoE (`--moe-backend aiter`, no shared-expert fusion). `--quantization-config.moe mxfp8` moves into the default variant, since only that checkpoint stores NVFP4 experts.
5. **Mono decode** (opt-in feature, MI355X + Quark only): a decode step of up to 16 tokens runs each layer as one kernel. Needs FP8 KV and indexer caches and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. On the released image (aiter 0.1.26) it also needs #63270, the backport of #61889, to start.
6. **Fixes**: one `fp8` variant, limited to Hopper (the merge of `main` had duplicated the key; on MI355X and Blackwell it rendered NVFP4 caches). VRAM minimums per GPU: the NVFP4 variant shows 285 GB, and MI355X gets 533 GB after the MXFP8 re-quantization.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes` passes on vllm-project/recipes `main`. Rendered commands were checked for the default, Quark, and FP8 variants on MI355X, B300, and H200, with and without the new features.
- Rendered commands served on MI355X TP4 with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`, DSpark 3, AIME26 (16 epochs, max_tokens 98304, thinking on) and MMMU-Pro (all, 3460):

  | command | AIME26 | MMMU-Pro |
  |---|---|---|
  | default (MXFP8 MoE) | 0.9351 x6 ¹ | 0.7676 x1 |
  | MXFP4 (Quark) | 0.9368 x6 | 0.7763 x1 |
  | MXFP4 (Quark) + mono decode, concurrency 4 | 0.9417 x8 | – |

  ¹ Same image, KV/indexer/MoE settings and DSpark 3, but served by our eval script (block verification), not the rendered command.

## Details

- The DBO / SP modes are offered on the default variant only (SP and SP + DBO were measured on the MXFP8 MoE); the Quark variant gets DBO.
- The recipe schema needs a mode per variant, so `mono_decode` carries an empty mode for the other variants: enabling it there changes nothing.
- The Quark MMMU run used `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": 0}'`. With video inputs on, one Quark server ran out of memory in the vision encoder at MMMU concurrency 256 (`--gpu-memory-utilization` 0.92).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the recipe changes and run the validation above; I reviewed the changes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek-VL2 cache identity across cropping modes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix DeepSeek-VL2 encoder-cache collisions when the same image appears in requests with different cropping modes.

## Claims

- Distinguish raw-image cache identities across cropping modes, including client-provided UUIDs.
- Preserve identities within each cropping mode and for precomputed image embeddings.

## Validation

uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_vl2.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_deepseek_vl2.py -q

6 passed. Tests cover cropping boundaries, content hashes, client-provided UUIDs, precomputed embeddings, and both single-image → three-image and reverse request sequences. Both generation cases failed before the fix.

Additional validation with real DeepSeek-VL2-tiny weights on an H800:

- Both request orders completed successfully.
- Alternating and repeated requests matched the eight-token outputs of corresponding successful requests on unpatched code. The repeated three-image request was compared against two consecutive three-image requests on unpatched code. Caching remained enabled.
- A subsequent text-only request succeeded.

## Details

DeepSeek-VL2 enables cropping for requests with at most two images and disables it for larger requests. The processor bypasses its preprocessing cache for larger requests, but still assigns the same image identity to different encoder outputs. In the reproducer, these outputs contained 1,023 and 421 embeddings.

Include the cropping mode in raw-image cache identities through _get_mm_hashes(). Precomputed image embeddings retain their existing identities.

commits.pr_title: [MM][Mistral] Use real-valued RoPE in the compiled Pixtral ViT
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `compile_mm_encoder` (#57168), the Mistral-format Pixtral ViT blocks still run the RoPE as a complex multiply. Inductor does not generate code for complex operators (`UserWarning: Torchinductor does not support code generation for complex operators. Performance may be worse than eager.`), so most of the compile gain is lost. This PR keeps the RoPE table as the real view of the complex frequencies and rotates q/k with real ops under `torch.compile`; eager mode keeps the complex multiply.

## Claims

- Compiled Pixtral ViT encoder is 8-25% faster than with the complex RoPE (Pixtral-12B, H100, one image).
- Eager mode is unchanged: same complex multiply, same numerics.
- No more "complex operators" fallback warning when compiling the Pixtral vision encoder.

## Validation

Encoder latency, `vllm bench mm-processor`, `mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409` (`--load-format dummy`), 1× H100, 1 image per request, 100 prompts, median `encoder_forward_ms`. Main and this branch were each run as Python sources over the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (one job per branch):

| image | main, eager | main, compile | this PR, eager | this PR, compile |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 512×512 | 15.11 ms | 10.78 ms | 15.78 ms | **8.05 ms** (−25%) |
| 1024×1024 | 20.97 ms | 15.97 ms | 21.76 ms | **14.63 ms** (−8%) |

The eager path is unchanged code-wise (the eager differences are within the run-to-run std of 0.9-2.2 ms). On main, the compile log has `Torchinductor does not support code generation for complex operators`; on this branch it does not.

<details><summary>Command</summary>

```
vllm bench mm-processor --model mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409 \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format dummy --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 1 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --dataset-name random-mm --num-prompts 100 --num-warmups 10 --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 1 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' --random-mm-bucket-config '{(1024,1024,1):1.0}' \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90 --seed 42 --compilation-config '{"compile_mm_encoder": true}'
```
</details>

Engine prefill throughput on a Pixtral-architecture OCR model (ViT: 16 layers, hidden 2048, head dim 64, patch 16; 1× H100, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, prompt = one square image, median of 2×5 iterations on one GPU), `compile_mm_encoder` vs eager:

| image | batch | before (complex RoPE) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1024 px | 32 | +3.3% (separate run) | +10.1% |
| 512 px | 32 | n/a | +15.4% |

End-to-end accuracy on the OCR model (4000-page internal OCR eval, greedy, compile + encoder CUDA graphs vs eager): page-content fuzzy match 0.9843 vs 0.9842, block fuzzy match 0.9500 vs 0.9497, bbox IoU 0.9660 vs 0.9657.

Tests:
- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_pixtral.py -k "not test_chat"`: 4 passed (new `test_real_rotary_emb_vit_matches_complex` checks the real path against the complex one).
- `pytest tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multimodal_compile.py -k pixtral`: 4 passed

The tests ran on this branch over the nightly image; the OCR-model numbers and eval ran on our vLLM fork (v0.31.0 + #57168 + #58182 + this change).

## Details

- `VisionTransformer.freqs_cis` now caches `torch.view_as_real(precompute_freqs_cis_2d(...))`, a float32 `(H, W, head_dim / 2, 2)` table. Indexing it gives `(num_patches, head_dim / 2, 2)`, which is what the compiled `TransformerBlock` receives (`freqs_cis` keeps dynamic dim 0). As a side effect, positions are no longer gathered from a complex tensor (the problem #49669 works around for NPU).
- `apply_rotary_emb_vit` dispatches on `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`. The all-real formulation in eager mode costs several elementwise kernels per tensor; we measured it ~14% slower than the complex multiply end to end on the OCR model, so eager keeps the complex path.
- Only the Mistral-format path (`PixtralForConditionalGeneration`) is touched; the HF path already uses cos/sin.
- Interaction with #56277 (Pixtral encoder CUDA graphs): its capture inputs build `rotary_freqs` as complex64 ones; with this PR they should be a real `(capacity, head_dim / 2, 2)` tensor with cos = 1, sin = 0. We run that combination internally (encoder graphs + this change) and can push the one-line adjustment to whichever PR lands second.

Duplicate check: no open PR changes the Pixtral ViT RoPE for torch.compile (searched "pixtral rope", "pixtral complex", "view_as_complex inductor"); #49669 only changes the gather for NPU.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Share non-streaming chat message assembly with batch derender
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Moves the non-streaming chat message assembly (which `tool_calls` to keep, `content` for forced tools, `include_reasoning`) into one helper that both `/v1/chat/completions` and batch derender call. Closes #57593, part of #42729.

## Claims

- New `assemble_chat_message_fields()` in `chat_completion/message_assembly.py`, used by `chat_completion_full_generator` and `OnlineDerenderer._parse_and_assemble`.
- No output change for `/v1/chat/completions` or `/cohere/v2/chat`. Serving still builds the message through `_create_chat_message` / `_finalize_response_message`.
- `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and generate `output_mode="derender"` now drop tool calls where coupled chat already did, instead of returning them:
  - Harmony (gpt-oss) with `tool_choice: "none"`. `HarmonyParser` doesn't gate on it and coupled chat dropped them since #30867.
  - Any tool parser with `tools` set and `tool_choice: null`.
  - Auto tools off or `"auto"` with no tools.
- Drops the now unused `ChatCompletionResponseChoice` branch from `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`.

## Validation

```bash
pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_message_assembly.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_include_reasoning.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_completion_with_function_calling.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere -q
```

New tests:
- `test_message_assembly.py`: unit tests for every branch, plus `include_reasoning`, `parallel_tool_calls=false` and tool call ID handling. No tokenizer needed.
- `test_derender_chat_drops_tool_calls_without_tool_choice`: batch derender with hermes + `tool_choice: null` and a stub parser that ignores `"none"`.
- `test_derender_text_choices_drops_tool_calls_without_tool_choice`: same for generate `output_mode="derender"`.
- `test_e2e_harmony_tool_choice_none_drops_tool_calls`: real gpt-oss render server, `"auto"` as a control.

No model eval. Generation is untouched and `/v1/chat/completions` output is the same. The derender change only picks which parser output to return.

No docs change. `docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md` already says derender gives the same `content` / `reasoning` / `tool_calls` split as `vllm serve`. This makes that true in more cases.

## Details

Serving and derender each had their own copy of the tool choice branching and derender's copy left out the "drop tool calls" branches. It relied on the parser to gate instead. Not every parser does: `HarmonyParser` ignores `"none"` and `AbstractParser` treats `null` as auto.

The helper takes the `Parser.parse()` output and returns the fields rather than a `ChatMessage`, so Cohere v2 can keep using its own message class. The parallel tool call filter now runs on the list before the message is built, not on the choice afterwards. `[:1]` of a non-empty list is still non-empty, so `finish_reason` doesn't change.

Not covered here: streaming (coupled streaming still keeps tool calls for Harmony `"none"` and for `null`), `role` and `echo` in derender. Those need their own issues.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Validate late-interaction mode and use count in the Python API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`LateInteractionParams` had no validation, and bad inputs fail in the worst places:

- An unknown `mode` string is silently skipped by the late-interaction runner (`_parse_late_interaction_meta` returns `None` for anything outside `cache_query`/`score_doc`), so a typo produces ordinary pooler output instead of an error.
- `cache_query` with `query_uses=None` crashes on the runner's `assert query_uses is not None`.
- `query_uses <= 0` poisons the cache lifecycle: the entry pops on the first `score_doc`, so the remaining paired documents fail with a cache miss.

`__post_init__` now rejects unknown modes and non-positive use counts, the same shape as the `LateChunkingParams.chunk_size` validation added in #63051. The HTTP scoring path builds these params programmatically with valid values (`build_late_interaction_query_params` / `build_late_interaction_doc_params`), so only hand-constructed Python-API requests change behavior.

This is not duplicating an existing PR: the only open late-interaction work is about cancelling cached queries (#56617) and request tracing (#61785), which are different seams.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/test_pooling_params.py -q
# 41 passed
```

The new rejection tests fail against unpatched main (10 failed: invalid mode and use-count values were silently accepted), while the valid-shape wire round-trip passes both before and after. CPU-only environment; no GPU run.

## AI assistance

This change was produced with AI assistance (Claude Code): the sibling gap was identified after #63051 landed, and the fix, tests, and verification above were run locally and reviewed line by line before submission.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fix DP NUMA affinity regression
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix CPU data-parallel ranks all binding to the same NUMA node, a regression from #45026. Fixes #47328.

## Claims

- With `--data-parallel-size N` on a multi-NUMA CPU host, each `EngineCore_DP*` now binds the cores and memory of its own NUMA node instead of every rank binding the same cores.
- Manual pinning with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES` without DP is unchanged.
- No change to shared engine code; the fix is CPU-only (26 lines added, 10 removed, excluding tests).

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue, on a 6-NUMA-node host:

```bash
vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --data-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 256
```

OpenMP binding chosen by each EngineCore at startup (from the `OpenMP thread binding info` log):

| | `EngineCore_DP0` | `EngineCore_DP1` |
|---|---|---|
| main | cores 192-222, reserved 223 | cores 192-222, reserved 223 (same) |
| this PR | cores 192-222 (node 0), reserved 223 | cores 224-254 (node 1), reserved 255 |

With this PR the two workers also bind memory to distinct NUMA nodes (`NUMA binding: Using MEMBIND policy ... nodes (0)` and `(1)`), and a completion request returns a correct response end to end.

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_cpu_resource_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py   # 21 passed
```

`test_omp_manager_binds_each_dp_rank_to_its_assigned_node` builds `OMPProcessManager` on a fake 2-node topology and checks that two DP ranks get disjoint cores. It fails (both ranks pick node 0 cores) if the assigned ids are ignored.

## Details

**Root cause.** #45026 moved the per-DP-rank device list from the device-control env var into `parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`. `CoreEngineProcManager` still computes each rank's shard and stores it there, and GPU/XPU consume it. The CPU code still read only `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`, which nothing sets per rank anymore. `OMPProcessManager`, which runs in the EngineCore process, then saw the full node list and picked `allowed_numa_nodes[local_rank]`, the same node for every DP rank.

**Fix.** `get_visible_memory_node()` takes an optional `assigned_node_ids`. Precedence is assigned ids, then `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`, then all nodes. `VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA` still overrides everything. Three call sites pass the ids:

- `OMPProcessManager` reads the config. The in-process `get_assigned_physical_gpu_ids()` global is only set inside worker processes, so it is not available in the EngineCore process where this runs.
- `CPUWorker` reads `vllm_config.parallel_config.assigned_physical_gpu_ids`.
- `CpuPlatform.get_current_memory_usage` runs in the worker and uses the global.

**Limitations.** `--device-ids` also fills `assigned_physical_gpu_ids`, so on CPU it now selects NUMA nodes (composed with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`), consistent with GPU. This path is not covered by the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't enable MM embedding inputs on KV consumers in language-model-only mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #56379, `_resolve_mm_embedding_inputs()` turns on `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` and `enable_mm_embeds` on every EC/KV consumer, including ones started with `--language-model-only`. This PR leaves both flags off on a KV-only consumer that sets `language_model_only` without `--enable-mm-embeds`, so a text-only KV consumer of a multimodal checkpoint runs in text-only mode again.

## Claims

- A language-model-only KV consumer (for example the decode instance of a text-only P/D deployment of a multimodal checkpoint) reports `supports_multimodal_inputs == False` again and no longer builds a `MultiModalBudget` or an HF processor in its scheduler, frontend and workers.
- This drops the host memory those processes have carried since #56379: about 3.4 GB per decode node in the deployment measured below.
- EPD consumers, the case #56379 targets, keep working: EC consumers always enable both flags, and a KV consumer still enables them unless it sets `language_model_only`. An EPD decode instance that uses `--language-model-only` to skip the encoder can opt back in with `--enable-mm-embeds`.

## Validation

**Unit.** New test `test_consumer_resolves_mm_embedding_inputs` in `tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py` (covered by the `tests/config` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`). It covers a KV consumer, a language-model-only KV consumer with and without `--enable-mm-embeds`, and a language-model-only EC consumer. Without the change, the language-model-only KV consumer case fails because `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` is `True`. All tests in the file and `pre-commit` pass (CPU-only container).

**Reproducer.** Start any multimodal checkpoint as a KV consumer in language-model-only mode, for example `--language-model-only --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' --kv-transfer-config '{..., "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}'`.
- Before: the frontend and workers log `enable_mm_embeds is True; modalities handled as embedding-only: ('image', 'video')`, and each EngineCore loads the HF processor.
- After: they log `All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0, running in text-only mode.`

**End to end.** Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, 1P1D on TPU (prefill PCP8, decode DP8 on one host each), served through vLLM 0.31.0 with the vllm-torchtpu platform plugin. Same image for both runs. Measured with an earlier revision that behaves identically for this decode configuration.

| decode node | without | with | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pod anonymous memory at serving start | 147.0 GB | 143.6 GB | **−3.4 GB** |
| EngineCore RSS (×8) | 1210 MiB | 802 MiB | −408 MiB each |
| API server RSS | 1743 MiB | 1325 MiB | −418 MiB |
| Worker RSS (×8, total) | 135.3 GiB | 135.5 GiB | unchanged |

The prefill node (KV producer) is unaffected. Serving with the change: 1003/1003 requests, 1503 tok/s, median TPOT 24.0 ms (4096-in / 512-out, concurrency 64, 5 min). I did not validate on GPU.

## Details

Path on the decode (KV consumer) instance of a text-only P/D deployment:

1. Decode starts with `kv_role=kv_consumer` and `--language-model-only`, so every modality limit is 0.
2. `VllmConfig._resolve_mm_embedding_inputs()` sets `allow_missing_mm_embeddings = True` (KV consumer) and then `enable_mm_embeds = True`.
3. `ModelConfig._supports_multimodal_inputs()` returns `True` despite the zero limits, because `enable_mm_embeds` is set.
4. `Scheduler.__init__` (and the frontend's `InputProcessor` and the workers) build a `MultiModalBudget`. `get_mm_max_toks_per_item()` calls e.g. `Qwen2VLProcessingInfo.get_max_image_tokens()` -> `get_image_processor()` -> `ctx.get_hf_processor()`, which instantiates the full HF processor (`Qwen3VLProcessor.from_pretrained`). That processor loads a second copy of the tokenizer and deep-copies it.

A KV role alone does not tell a text-only P/D decode instance from an EPD one, so the change uses `language_model_only` as the text-only signal.

commits.pr_title: [Security][CI/Build] Bump uv to 0.13.4 in CI scripts for eMudhra CA distrust
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #62868 (eMudhra CA compromise): bump the Rust CI script's uv pin to 0.13.4, the fixed version in [Python's guidance](https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576), and fix the release script's uv pin, which currently has no effect.

## Claims

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make online FP8 MoE experts batch-invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #57016

## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a MoE model served with `--quantization fp8` (online per-tensor FP8, Triton experts) still produces output that depends on which other requests share its batch: greedy tokens flip within the first ~10 positions and prefix-cached K/V differs depending on who wrote it. Dense layers are invariant; only the experts are not.

Two things were wrong:

1. `Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod` (and `Fp8MoEMethod` for FP8-serialized per-tensor checkpoints with dynamic activations) quantize the expert inputs with one dynamic scale over the whole activation tensor (`kFp8DynamicTensorSym`), i.e. the max over every token of every co-batched request. Under batch-invariant mode this PR selects `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and passes `per_act_token_quant=True`, mirroring what `Fp8LinearMethod` already does for dense layers.
2. Switching to per-token activations exposed a latent launcher bug: `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` passed `stride_bse=0` for 1-D `[E]` weight scales (and `stride_bsn=1` for the singleton dim of `[E, 1, 1]`), so the kernel's `per_channel_quant` branch read expert 0's scale for every expert or indexed past the buffer. The combination tests already skipped "per-tensor weights + per-token activations" for the Triton experts as NYI, although `TritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` advertises the pair. This PR passes the expert stride unconditionally and broadcasts singleton scale dims, and narrows the NYI gate to the still-unsupported "per-channel weights + per-tensor activations" case so the combination suite covers the fixed pair.

The bf16 Triton expert path is already invariant on `main` (`get_default_config`/`get_moe_configs` pin the tile config under the flag); the reporter's bf16 mismatch was on 0.27.1.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_online_fp8_moe_logprobs_bitwise_bs1_vs_bsN` (granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct, `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, greedy, BS=1 vs BS=8 bitwise tokens+logprobs). Fails on `main`, passes with this PR.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: the per-tensor-weight + per-token-activation FP8 config is no longer skipped for `TritonExperts` / `BatchedTritonExperts` / `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts`.
- Reporter's reproducer (co-batch and writer-suffix modes) against a running server.
- Kernel check: `fused_experts` vs `tests.kernels.utils.torch_experts`, E=32, N=1024, K=2048, M=128, topk=4, per-tensor `[E,1,1]` weight scales: max abs err 0.010 with per-tensor activations, 0.003 with per-token activations (before the launcher fix the per-token case returned values in the thousands).
- Existing suites: `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_fused_moe`, pre-commit, `mypy-3.12`.

Hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), WSL2, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The modular kernel combination suite itself does not run on this WSL2 machine (spawned worker fails with `CUDA error: invalid resource handle` on unmodified `main` too), so that part relies on CI and on the independent H20 run linked below.

## Test Result

- Reporter's probe, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 --quantization fp8`, before: A-alone vs A-with-B first token flip at 11 (logprob gap 0.166), warm-vs-cold flip at 11 (gap 0.347). After: every comparison identical, both rounds.
- gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` (tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py): default (no flag) 34.1%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on `main` 34.3%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with this PR 32.7%. Per-token activation quantization is strictly finer than per-tensor, and the kernel-level error is lower, so the small delta is sampling noise from a 1B model.
- New e2e test: PASS with the PR, FAIL on `main` ("logprobs are not bitwise equal between BS=1 and BS=8; max abs diff 2.2e-01").
- Independent cross-architecture validation by @CarrotSwordsman on H20 (sm_90, real Linux GPU, driver 535), [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57092#issuecomment-5730213177): the same e2e test FAILS on a clean 0.28.0+cu129 wheel (max abs diff 2.8e-01) and PASSES with this PR's files applied, reproducing and eliminating the #57016 symptom on Hopper. Their `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` run on the patched wheel was 8 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, the two failures being `deep_gemm`'s `NVCC >= 12.3` assert in a container pinned to 12.1. As they note, that suite does not discriminate against a release wheel (the pre-PR NYI skip is not present there to be removed), so the e2e pair is the evidence in that setup.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` (non-DeepGEMM): 164 passed, 20 skipped. `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k test_fused_moe`: 241 passed. pre-commit and `mypy-3.12` clean on all changed files.

> Note: since #53585, online per-tensor FP8 is selected with `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`; commands above that use `--quantization fp8` predate that change.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #57016 (checked with `gh pr list --search "57016 in:body"` and by searching open PRs for "batch invariant moe"); #55881 is the XPU MoE variant and does not touch the CUDA Triton path or FP8 activation quantization.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] shm_broadcast: poll the notify socket from busy readers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63026. A local SHM reader that keeps reading (which is the normal state under load) never touches its `CONFLATE` notify socket, and libzmq queues an internal command for every write notification until it does. Reader memory then grows with every message. This PR polls the notify socket from `SpinCondition.record_read()` at most once per second.

## Claims

- Reader-side memory stays bounded under sustained load. Before this change, every message added ~41 B to the reader's libzmq mailbox. That affects each worker's RPC broadcast reader (2 messages per step) and EngineCore's response readers (one per replying worker; all of them reply when a KV connector is used).
- The SHM data path, notification semantics, idle wake-up and shutdown are unchanged. The added cost is one `poll(timeout=0)` per reader per second.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `test_busy_reader_consumes_write_notifications` fails without the fix and passes with it.

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py -q   # 59 passed, 2 skipped
```

**E2E (GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, TP=2, 128 prompts × 8192 tokens, `ignore_eos`).** Right after `generate()`, before any reader goes idle, the script below calls `getsockopt(ZMQ_EVENTS)` on every local reader's notify socket and records how much heap that frees. The freed heap is the size of the queued backlog.

| process | local readers | upstream backlog | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| EngineCore | 2 | 311.6 KiB (~7.8K cmds) | ≈0 (-0.8 KiB, noise) |
| worker 0 | 1 | 300.2 KiB (~7.5K cmds) | ≈0 (-2.2 KiB) |
| worker 1 | 2 | 298.4 KiB (~7.5K cmds) | ≈0 (-5.6 KiB) |

`generate()` took 46.4 s on upstream and 46.5 s with this PR. At this step rate (~5.7 ms), upstream grows by ~23 MiB/h per process, and the backlog is never cleared while the engine stays busy. That is about one command per step rather than two: `sample_tokens` follows `execute_model` within ~3 ms, so the writer's `SNDHWM=1` usually drops its notification on aarch64.

<details>
<summary>e2e_notify_backlog.py</summary>

```python
"""E2E check for vllm#63026: notify-socket command backlog under sustained decode.

Runs a TP=2 engine (EngineCore in-process) that never idles for >1s, then
immediately makes libzmq process the queued commands on every local SHM reader
notify socket and reports the freed heap. ~41 B per queued command.
"""

import argparse
import os
import time

os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD", "fork")


def heap_in_use() -> int:
    import ctypes
    import re
    import tempfile

    libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6")
    libc.fopen.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
    libc.fopen.argtypes = [ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_char_p]
    libc.fclose.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
    libc.malloc_info.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p]
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".xml") as f:
        fp = libc.fopen(f.name.encode(), b"w")
        libc.malloc_info(0, fp)
        libc.fclose(fp)
        tail = open(f.name).read()
    tail = tail[tail.rfind("</heap>") :]

    def total(t):
        m = re.search(rf'<total type="{t}" count="\d+" size="(\d+)"', tail)
        return int(m.group(1))

    system = int(re.search(r'<system type="current" size="(\d+)"', tail).group(1))
    return system - total("fast") - total("rest") + total("mmap")


def find_readers(holder, baseline):
    import gc

    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators import shm_broadcast

    if baseline:
        shm_broadcast.SHM_NOTIFY_POLL_INTERVAL_S = float("inf")
    # vLLM gc.freeze()s after startup; frozen objects are hidden from get_objects.
    frozen = gc.get_freeze_count() > 0
    gc.unfreeze()
    holder._issue_63026_readers = [
        o
        for o in gc.get_objects()
        if isinstance(o, shm_broadcast.MessageQueue)
        and getattr(o, "_is_local_reader", False)
    ]
    if frozen:
        gc.freeze()
    return len(holder._issue_63026_readers)


def drain(holder):
    import os

    import zmq

    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators import shm_broadcast

    readers = holder._issue_63026_readers
    before = heap_in_use()
    for mq in readers:
        mq._spin_condition.local_notify_socket.getsockopt(zmq.EVENTS)
    freed = before - heap_in_use()
    return dict(
        pid=os.getpid(),
        readers=len(readers),
        freed_kib=freed / 1024,
        approx_cmds=freed // 41,
        interval=shm_broadcast.SHM_NOTIFY_POLL_INTERVAL_S,
    )


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
    p.add_argument("--tp", type=int, default=2)
    p.add_argument("--num-prompts", type=int, default=128)
    p.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=8192)
    p.add_argument(
        "--baseline", action="store_true", help="disable the fix (upstream behavior)"
    )
    args = p.parse_args()

    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    llm = LLM(model=args.model, tensor_parallel_size=args.tp)
    executor = llm.llm_engine.engine_core.engine_core.model_executor

    class Main:
        pass

    main_holder = Main()
    print("readers:", find_readers(main_holder, args.baseline),
          llm.collective_rpc(find_readers, args=(args.baseline,)))

    params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=args.max_tokens, ignore_eos=True)
    prompts = [f"Write a long story about number {i}." for i in range(args.num_prompts)]
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0

    # Measure before any reader goes idle (>1s) and polls on its own.
    engine = drain(main_holder)
    workers = executor.collective_rpc(drain)

    tag = "baseline" if args.baseline else "fix"
    print(f"\n[{tag}] generate {elapsed:.1f}s, ~{args.max_tokens} decode steps")
    print(f"[{tag}] engine-core: {engine}")
    for w in workers:
        print(f"[{tag}] worker     : {w}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run with `python e2e_notify_backlog.py --baseline` and then `python e2e_notify_backlog.py`. The `--baseline` flag sets the interval to `inf`, which disables the fix and gives upstream behavior.
</details>

**Standalone `MessageQueue`.** One writer and one busy reader, aarch64, pyzmq 27.1 / libzmq 4.3.5. The table shows reader heap growth per message.

| writer gap | upstream | poll+recv every 1s (this PR) | `recv(NOBLOCK)` only, every 1s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 ms | 42.6 B/msg | 1.3 B/msg | – |
| 2 ms | 21.5 B/msg | 1.1 B/msg | 21.5 B/msg (no effect) |

At a 2 ms gap, about half of the notifications are dropped by the writer's `SNDHWM=1` (see #58917), so fewer commands reach the reader.

## Details

**Root cause.** In libzmq 4.3.5, `ypipe_conflate_t::flush()` returns `reader_awake`, and nothing ever sets that to true. A `CONFLATE` session pipe also gets HWM -1 (unlimited). So for every notification it receives, the reader's I/O thread posts an `activate_read` command to the SUB socket's mailbox. Those commands are only processed when the application calls into the socket. libzmq documents this under `ZMQ_CONFLATE` in `zmq_setsockopt(3)`: "If recv is not called on the inbound socket, the queue and memory will grow with each message received. Use ZMQ_EVENTS to trigger the conflation of the messages." `SpinCondition.wait()` polls only after `busy_loop_s` (1 s) without a read, which never happens while the engine is stepping. The backlog is cleared only after the reader idles for more than 1 s. EngineCore's response readers stay stuck until the next request arrives, and RSS may not come back down even then.

**Why `poll()` and not just `recv()`.** When a message is already in the pipe, `recv(NOBLOCK)` returns it without processing commands, so the backlog keeps growing (last column in the standalone table above). `poll()` goes through `ZMQ_EVENTS`, which processes them.

**Correctness.** Notifications are only wake-up hints; the SHM flags are authoritative. The writer always sets the written flag (with a fence) before it notifies. So if a busy read consumes a notification, the slot it announced is already visible to the next `acquire_read()` check. The socket is only used by the reader thread, the same thread that runs `wait()`. Cancellation goes through a separate socket.

**Interval.** 1 s matches the default `busy_loop_s` and the interval used by vllm-project/vllm-ascend#19140, which is the Ascend-side workaround for the same issue. That patch can be dropped once this lands. At most ~1 s worth of commands can accumulate. I kept the interval as a separate constant instead of reusing `busy_loop_s`, because #52814 would make that window configurable down to ~0.

**Not a duplicate.** #58917 changes the writer's HWM so that notifications are not dropped. It does not touch the reader mailbox, and it would actually remove the incidental rate cap that currently limits this growth. #52814 and #52848 change the busy window and sleep. No open PR services the reader's notify socket.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Fix weight cache daemon GPU memory and warm-cache warmup hang
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes three issues with the weight cache daemon (`vllm preload`) that made fast start differ from a disk load, plus one logging issue.

1. **The KV cache was smaller than with a disk load.** `get_memory` reported `torch.accelerator.memory_allocated()`. That number also counts memory the engine never maps: communication buffers, warmup workspaces, and tensors outside parameters/buffers, which the engine rebuilds itself and so pays for twice. The engine subtracts the reported number from its `gpu_memory_utilization` budget. The daemon now reports the bytes of the distinct CUDA storages it exports.
2. **The daemon held its process groups for its whole lifetime.** Serving only exports CUDA IPC handles, but the NCCL / custom all-reduce / symm-mem communicators and the FlashInfer all-reduce workspace kept about 2.5 GiB per GPU pinned outside the engine's budget. The daemon now tears them down after warmup.
3. **Warmup deadlocked with a warm compile cache (TP > 1).** The daemon never set `parallel_config.rank`, so every daemon used `torch_aot_compile/<hash>/rank_0_0`. With a warm cache, all ranks loaded rank 0's artifact, whose Inductor code hard-codes `set_device(0)`. Warmup lazily creates the FlashInfer MNNVL workspace inside that graph, so on ranks 1..N it used `torch.cuda.current_device() == 0`:
   - On those ranks, `cuMulticastAddDevice` failed with `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` and they fell back to the trtllm workspace.
   - Rank 0 kept waiting in `cuMemMap` for the other ranks to add their devices.

   The daemon now sets `parallel_config.rank` the way engine workers do (`worker_base.py`).

   Caches written before this fix may still contain such an artifact under `rank_0_0`. Clear the daemon's `torch_aot_compile` cache once after upgrading.
4. **Logs were dropped in the daemon processes.** The spawned daemons never called `configure_logging`, so their vLLM logs were lost.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "not cold_start and not rope_matching"`, including two new tests:
  - `test_daemon_reports_exported_weight_bytes`
  - `test_daemon_sets_its_rank_like_engine_workers`
- End to end on 4x B300: Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`, `--max-model-len 8192`, `--load-format ipc_cache` in zero_copy mode.
  - Ran the daemon with both a cold and a warm compile cache.
  - Compared the KV cache, the daemon's GPU memory, and a greedy completion against a disk load.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 9 passed. `test_ipc_rope_matching` fails the same way on `main`, so it is unrelated to this change.

| | disk load | daemon before | daemon after |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV cache | 152.71 GiB / 13,343,600 tokens | 152.61 GiB / 13,335,648 tokens | 152.73 GiB / 13,345,760 tokens |
| Weights charged to the engine | 4.29 GiB loaded | 4.35 GiB | 4.24 GiB |
| Daemon GPU memory | - | 8,244 MiB | 5,698 MiB |
| Warmup with a warm compile cache | - | hung 4/4 | ready 2/2 (cold and warm) |

- The greedy completion matched the disk load exactly.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Muse Spark: apply output multiplier and softcap in compute_logits_local
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, the ROCm Muse Spark model samples from logits that skip its output multiplier and final-logit softcap. This PR gives the model its own `compute_logits_local`, which applies the same transform as `compute_logits`. Follow-up to #62622.

## Claims

- With batch-sharded sampling, ROCm Muse Spark samples from the same fp32 logits as the default path: multiplier 32^-0.5 and softcap 20 are applied.
- With batch-sharded sampling off, which is the default, behavior is unchanged. `compute_logits` only moves its existing post-processing into a helper that both methods call.

## Validation

The new test calls `compute_logits_local` and `compute_logits` on the same hidden states and requires identical output. It fails on the base commit and passes with this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py -q      # base 2de0531d81
E   AssertionError: The values for attribute 'dtype' do not match: torch.bfloat16 != torch.float32.
FAILED tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py::test_compute_logits_local_applies_output_transform
1 failed

$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py -q      # this PR
1 passed
```

On the base commit the inherited method returns the raw bf16 lm_head output, so the comparison fails on dtype before it reaches the values. The existing Muse tests also pass with this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py -q
21 passed
```

These runs were CPU-only, in the ROCm image with no GPU attached. Because of that, the ROCm architecture query and device detection were stubbed locally. The new test is wired into the "Basic Models (Other)" Buildkite step and its MI355 mirror. The MI355 mirror now also lists `vllm/models/muse_spark/` as a dependency.

**Not yet done:** an end-to-end GPU run with `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, and a model evaluation such as GSM8K comparing the flag on and off. Both are needed before this PR leaves draft.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- The GPU model runner enables batch-sharded sampling for any model that has a `compute_logits_local` attribute (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:447-448`).
- In the sampling step it then calls that method and runs an all-to-all instead of calling `compute_logits` (`model_runner.py:1633`).
- The ROCm `MuseSpark1xForCausalLM` inherits `LlamaForCausalLM.compute_logits_local` (`vllm/model_executor/models/llama.py:553`), which returns raw lm_head logits.
- Muse's `compute_logits` (`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:1096`) casts to fp32 and applies the multiplier and softcap. The batch-sharded path skipped all of that.
- Greedy decoding is unaffected, because both transforms preserve order. Sampled decoding and speculative-decoding rejection sampling used the wrong distribution.

**Fix.** The transform is elementwise, so applying it to each rank's vocab shard before the all-to-all gives exactly the logits `compute_logits` produces. The runner trims vocab padding after the all-to-all. A generic guard in the model runner was considered and rejected, to keep core code untouched.

**Not a duplicate.** No other open PR changes `compute_logits_local` for Muse Spark. #63078 touches Muse RoPE, not logits.

**Test limitation.** The test builds the model with `__new__` and sets the attributes `compute_logits` reads, instead of using the real constructor. Building a real Muse Spark model needs TP state and the full checkpoint config. This conflicts with `tests/AGENTS.md`'s preference for real constructors, and is noted for reviewers.

## GSM8K: batch-sharded sampling with and without this PR

**Setup.** 8x MI355X, TP8, `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, no speculative decoding. Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-df6603f05` (aiter 0.1.26, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0), with each tree's Python overlaid; base is main 2de0531d81. Server flags are the AMD MXFP4 recipe's:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --language-model-only --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 [--enable-batch-sharded-sampling]

# 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, max 256 tokens, 64 concurrent requests
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --temperature 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --temperature 1.0 --seed 42
```

Accuracy is shown ± one binomial standard error (n = 1,319). Sampled runs also use the model's default `top_k` 64 from its generation config.

| Code | `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` | Greedy accuracy | Sampled accuracy, T=1.0 | Sampled output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main 2de0531d81 | off | 0.9507 ± 0.0060 | 0.8196 ± 0.0106 | 142,640 |
| main 2de0531d81 | on | 0.9462 ± 0.0062 | **0.9469 ± 0.0062** | 123,631 |
| this PR | on | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | **0.8067 ± 0.0109** | 143,352 |

All three servers start with the same KV cache (167.67 GiB, 8,173,209 tokens). Both flag-on servers log `Batch-sharded sampling enabled.` on all 8 ranks.

- **Greedy is unaffected.** All three greedy scores agree within one standard error, as expected: the multiplier and softcap preserve the order of the logits.
- **On main, the flag silently breaks sampling.** The temperature-1.0 run scores 0.9469 with 123,631 output tokens. That matches the greedy run (0.9462, 123,688 tokens) and is 12.7 points above main with the flag off. Without the 32^-0.5 multiplier the logits are about 5.7x too large, which acts like a temperature of about 0.18, so requested sampling becomes nearly greedy.
- **This PR restores the expected distribution.** With the flag on, the sampled score (0.8067) and output length (143,352 tokens) match main with the flag off (0.8196, 142,640 tokens). The 1.3-point gap is within 1 combined standard error.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Forward the configured cpu distributed timeout to `cpu_all_reduce_`
commits.pr_body:
## Overview


#61767 introduced `cpu_all_reduce_` (`vllm/distributed/utils.py`), a low-latency gloo all-reduce for the DP hot path — `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state` (engine-side DP state sync) and `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (worker-side DP padding/cudagraph coordination). It replaced `torch.distributed.all_reduce` with raw `group.send`/`group.recv` p2p ops waited on via bare `work.wait()`.

A bare `wait()` never times out: the gloo group's default timeout is not applied to these p2p waits. So since #61767, `--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds` silently no longer takes effect on the DP sync path — when a DP peer hangs or dies, the surviving ranks block inside the DP sync, where previously they would have raised a timeout error.

## Claims


Now `cpu_all_reduce_` will throw timeout error under defined `-cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds`.


## Validation



**Unit test** : `pytest tests/distributed/test_cpu_all_reduce.py`

`test_cpu_all_reduce_timeout` spawns 2 gloo ranks; rank 1 never joins the all-reduce, and rank 0 calls `cpu_all_reduce_` with `timeout=timedelta(seconds=1)`. It asserts a `RuntimeError("Timed out ...")` is raised and that the call returns in under 3s (measured ~1.0s), i.e. the wait honors the timeout rather than hanging until the peer process exits.

**Manual e2e**: launched a DP=2 deployment, put one DP rank to sleep, and observed the other rank raise the gloo timeout in the DP sync within the configured window instead of hanging.


## Details



Add an optional `timeout: timedelta | None = None` parameter and forward it to every p2p `work.wait(timeout)`:

- `cpu_all_reduce_` — bounds each p2p wait; `None` keeps the previous no-timeout behavior, so other callers are unaffected.
- `GroupCoordinator.cpu_all_reduce_` and `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state` — pass-through plumbing.
- Both DP call sites now forward the configured `cpu_distributed_timeout`: `DPEngineCoreProc._has_global_unfinished_reqs` (engine DP state sync) and `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (worker DP sync).

With this, a hung peer surfaces as a `RuntimeError("Timed out ...")` on the surviving ranks within the configured timeout, instead of an indefinite hang.

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Add GELU-tanh MoE, FP8 checkpoint support and Gemma-4 INT8 TP=4 padding
commits.pr_body:
## Summary
Two independent CPU-backend changes:

- **GELU-tanh MoE activation:** `amd/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w8a8-llmcompressor` uses `gelu_pytorch_tanh` in its MoE blocks, but every SGL-kernel-backed CPU MoE path (INT8/INT4/FP8 W8A8, FP8/MXFP4 W8A16) only supported SiLU. Partially syncs the vendored SGLang CPU kernels to get the generic `CPUActMethod` dispatch (4 files with unrelated upstream changes are left unsynced, noted in `common.h`), adds an AVX512 `gelu_tanh_and_mul` primitive, and threads it through all 5 `CPUQuantMethod` kernels, the `fused_experts_cpu` op schema, and each `CPUExperts*` class. `_supports_activation` of each class now matches what its kernel implements (`CPUExpertsFp8`/`CPUExpertsMxfp4` also declare exact GELU), and the activation is passed to `fused_experts_cpu` as a `CPUActMethod` IntEnum (mapped explicitly from `MoEActivation`) instead of a string, so clamped swiglu (`SWIGLUOAI`) is selected explicitly rather than inferred from alpha/limit. DeepSeek-style shared-expert kernels are untouched. Also makes this model work at TP=4: the MoE intermediate size 704 shards to 176 per rank, which the INT8 kernel rejected (it needs a multiple of 32), so `CPUExpertsInt8` now zero-pads the intermediate dim (weights and w13 scale) before prepacking, reusing the padding the unquantized CPU experts already do.
- **FP8 checkpoints on CPU:** `static_scaled_fp8_quant` and `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` were placeholders that raised on CPU, so any path calling `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` failed (load-time requantization of fused modules, online FP8 quantization, Torch FP8 linear fallbacks). Implements both with AVX-512 (e4m3fn/e5m2, 0D/1D/2D static scales, per-token dynamic scales with `scale_ub`), and adds `CPUFp8ChannelWiseScaledMMLinearKernel` so per-channel FP8 weights (e.g. `*-FP8-dynamic` checkpoints) run through the SGL W8A16 kernel.

## Changes
- GELU-tanh MoE: `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/{common,gemm,moe,moe_fp8,moe_fp8_w8a8,moe_int4,moe_int8,vec}.*`, `csrc/cpu/torch_bindings.cpp`, `vllm/_custom_ops.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/cpu_moe.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py` (TP=4 padding test).
- FP8 on CPU: `csrc/cpu/fp8_quant.cpp`, `cmake/cpu_extension.cmake`, `csrc/cpu/torch_bindings.cpp`, `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/{__init__,scaled_mm/cpu}.py`, `tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_{quant,scaled_mm}.py`, `.buildkite/hardware_tests/cpu.yaml` (runs the new FP8 quant tests in the CPU kernel job).

## Test plan
- [x] Rebuilt at the PR head and ran `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py`, `tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_quant.py` and `tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_scaled_mm.py`: 666 passed, 318 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] GELU-tanh: new tests for all 5 quant configs against a plain-PyTorch reference. End-to-end on `amd/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w8a8-llmcompressor`: the INT8 CPU MoE backend is selected and a `temperature=0.0` chat prompt answers correctly ("The capital of France is Paris."). At TP=4 (previously `No Int8 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration`) the same model selects the CPU INT8 MoE backend and answers chat prompts correctly (`The capital of France is Paris.`, `42`); the new padding test compares against the unpadded reference for an intermediate size of 176 and fails (`invalid weight input features 176`) with the padding disabled.
- [x] FP8 on CPU: full GSM8K (1319 questions) on RedHatAI `Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8`, `Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic` and `Qwen3-4B-FP8-dynamic`. AVX-512 quant ops vs. the scalar loops on a Xeon 6972P (32 threads), 2048x4096 bf16: static 433 -> 123 us, per-token 772 -> 177 us. The e4m3fn conversion is bit-identical to `c10::Float8_e4m3fn` over every bf16/fp16 bit pattern and 4M random fp32 values.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Watermarking: skip greedy-fallback argmax when no request is greedy
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`GPUWatermarkSampler._sample_random` ran a full-vocabulary argmax on every watermarked step to give greedy (temperature 0) rows their token, even when the batch had no greedy row. This PR checks the host-side temperatures first and skips the argmax and the `torch.where` when no row is greedy.

## Claims

- The watermarked sampler step is 13 to 41 µs faster under CUDA graphs on H200 (B = 1 to 128, vocab 151,936), for both `gumbel` and `dual_key_gumbel`. That is 15 to 22% of the step, and 17 to 41% of the watermark's overhead over the plain sampler.
- Serving Qwen3-0.6B with Gumbel watermarking at concurrency 32: mean TPOT drops by 21.5 ± 11.5 µs (6 paired replicates), which matches the 20 µs saved per step at B = 32. The no-watermark arm does not change.
- Speculative decoding (`dual_key_gumbel` + DFlash): the verify step uses the rejection sampler, which handles greedy rows inside its kernel and never reaches the changed code. Verify-step time and serving throughput are unchanged. Only steps where no request in the batch has drafts go through `_sample_random`; those get the same saving.
- Sampled tokens are unchanged. When any row is greedy, the old code runs as before.

## Validation

![Sampler step time before and after, CUDA graph replay, H200](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/5571ba41e2321317fe8f5c7357b7031ffd9b43b4/sampler_step_before_after.png)

**Tests.** `pytest tests/watermarking tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py` on 1x H200: 229 passed, 3 skipped, both before and after this change (the skips are the 2-GPU tests). `tests/watermarking/test_parallel_compatibility.py` on 2x H200: 3 passed. The new `test_gpu_sampler_uses_argmax_only_for_greedy_rows` checks one greedy plus one watermarked row (greedy row gets the argmax) and two watermarked rows (both keep the watermarked token). It also passes against the old `gpu_sampler.py`, so the tokens match the previous behaviour. `tests/watermarking` runs in the CPU `watermarking` CI step.

**Microbenchmark, sampler step.** CUDA graph replay, µs, 1x H200. fp32 logits, vocab 151,936, temperature 1, no top-k/top-p, context width 4, `deduplicate_contexts=single_turn`. Before and after interleaved, 3 rounds, mean of the per-round medians (round-to-round sd ≤ 0.4 µs).

| Step | B | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `gumbel` | 1 | 72.7 | 59.3 | −13.4 (−18%) |
| `gumbel` | 32 | 98.7 | 78.5 | −20.2 (−20%) |
| `gumbel` | 128 | 185.9 | 144.6 | −41.3 (−22%) |
| `dual_key_gumbel` | 1 | 90.8 | 77.5 | −13.3 (−15%) |
| `dual_key_gumbel` | 32 | 135.4 | 114.5 | −20.9 (−15%) |
| `dual_key_gumbel` | 128 | 280.2 | 239.1 | −41.0 (−15%) |
| Spec decode, step without drafts (`dual_key_gumbel` target) | 1 | 73.4 | 60.4 | −13.1 (−18%) |
| Spec decode, step without drafts | 32 | 96.9 | 76.9 | −20.0 (−21%) |
| Spec decode, step without drafts | 128 | 184.7 | 143.2 | −41.5 (−22%) |
| Spec decode, verify step (3 drafts, B × 4 rows) | 1 | 73.4 | 73.4 | −0.1 |
| Spec decode, verify step | 32 | 149.5 | 149.2 | −0.3 |
| Spec decode, verify step | 128 | 326.8 | 326.6 | −0.2 |
| No watermark (`Sampler._sample_random`) | 1 / 32 / 128 | 13.3 / 31.2 / 85.2 | 13.1 / 31.3 / 85.3 | ±0.2 |

The verify row times `RejectionSampler._verify` with watermarking. In that benchmark `_sample_random` is replaced by a stub that raises, which confirms the verify step never calls it. In eager mode the step is launch-bound (about 350 to 540 µs) and the two skipped launches save 10 to 40 µs.

**Serving, Gumbel.** Qwen3-0.6B, 1x H200 per replicate, random 1024 in / 128 out, 1000 prompts, concurrency 32, T = 1.0, `--ignore-eos`, `--watermark-config '{"algorithm":"gumbel","key":42,"context_width":4}'`. A fresh server per arm, one discarded warm-up bench, then the median of 3 benches. Arm order rotated, server and client pinned to the GPUs' NUMA node. 6 paired replicates, mean ± SE of the paired difference:

| Comparison | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gumbel, after − before | +38 ± 33 | −21.5 ± 11.5 µs |
| No watermark, after − before | −16 ± 11 | −5.8 ± 5.2 µs |
| Gumbel overhead over no watermark, before | −292 ± 21 (−3.3%) | +114.6 ± 7.8 µs |
| Gumbel overhead over no watermark, after | −238 ± 14 (−2.7%) | +98.9 ± 5.9 µs |

The TPOT gain is about 0.7% for this small model, close to run-to-run noise. The microbenchmark is the main evidence.

**Serving, speculative decoding.** Qwen3-8B with `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (`dflash`, 3 speculative tokens, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`), `--watermark-config '{"algorithm":"dual_key_gumbel","key":42,"alpha":0.1}'`, same client and protocol as above. Arms: no watermark, before, after. 3 paired replicates, each on its own H200, mean ± SE of the paired difference:

| Comparison | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Watermarked, after − before | +0.8 ± 0.2 (+0.03%) | +14.0 ± 14.5 µs (+0.13%) | 1.74 → 1.74 |
| Watermark vs no watermark, before | +28.5 ± 0.7 (+1.0%) | −145 ± 8 µs | 1.67 → 1.74 |
| Watermark vs no watermark, after | +29.3 ± 0.9 (+1.1%) | −131 ± 7 µs | 1.67 → 1.74 |

Arm means: no watermark 2760 tok/s / 10.83 ms TPOT, before 2788 / 10.69, after 2789 / 10.70. Spec-decode serving does not change, as the code path predicts. (On this random-token workload the watermarked arms run slightly faster than no watermark because their acceptance length is higher.) A seeded completion produced the same text before and after.

**No GPU syncs.** Serving Qwen3-0.6B with Gumbel watermarking under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed 200 of 200 requests with no sync error.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

Before = upstream main `b7701fc3e4`; after = this branch. The "before" runs used the branch checkout with upstream main's `vllm/v1/watermarking/gpu_sampler.py` overlaid through `PYTHONPATH`; each run logged which file it imported.

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1

# Tests
pytest tests/watermarking tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py
pytest tests/watermarking/test_parallel_compatibility.py   # 2 GPUs

# Serving, Gumbel (arms: with and without --watermark-config)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --watermark-config '{"algorithm":"gumbel","key":42,"context_width":4}'

# Serving, speculative decoding (arms: with and without --watermark-config)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --watermark-config '{"algorithm":"dual_key_gumbel","key":42,"alpha":0.1}'

# Client (one warm-up run, then 3 measured runs per server)
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model <model> --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 1000 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 32 --temperature 1.0 --seed 1
```

The microbenchmarks call `GPUWatermarkSampler._sample_random`, `Sampler._sample_random` and `RejectionSampler._verify` directly with real vLLM code and synthetic state (prompt 1024, 64 generated tokens, random token history), and time them with `triton.testing.do_bench` on a captured CUDA graph.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The greedy fallback was unconditional:

```python
sampled = torch.where(temperatures == 0, processed_logits.argmax(dim=-1), sampled)
```

The argmax reads the whole `[B, V]` fp32 logits tensor again after the watermark kernel has already read it. At B = 32 and V = 151,936 that is 19.4 MB per step, plus a second kernel launch for `torch.where`. Most watermarked traffic has no greedy rows, because a greedy request cannot be watermarked, so the result was usually discarded.

**Change.** Run the fallback only if `self.sampling_states.any_greedy(idx_mapping_np)` is true. This existing helper reads the host-side temperature array, the same one `_sample_random` already reads to decide whether watermarking is on for the batch. The branch is decided on the host, like the existing watermarking-enabled check above it, so there is no GPU sync. Expanded (speculative) rows repeat `idx_mapping` rows, so the host check covers them too.

**Speculative decoding.** When the batch has drafts, the V2 model runner calls `RejectionSampler`. It applies sampling params and runs the watermarked `rejection_sample` kernels, which handle temperature-0 rows in-kernel (accept if the draft matches the target argmax). It does not call `_sample_random`. The draft side (`DraftWatermarker.sample`) has no greedy-fallback argmax either. So this PR only affects spec-decode steps where no request in the batch has drafts. In the DFlash serving run above, 13 of the first 5,000 sampling steps (0.3%, startup warm-up included) went through `_sample_random`, counted with a diagnostic hook; the rest used the rejection sampler.

**Behaviour.** Tokens are unchanged for every batch. One internal difference: padding rows (`expanded_idx_mapping == -1`) used to read slot −1's temperature on the GPU and could receive an argmax token. They now keep the sampled token when no real row is greedy. Padding rows are discarded, so this is not observable.

**Tests.** Three existing tests stub `sampler.sampling_states` with a `SimpleNamespace`; they get an `any_greedy` stub that returns `False`, since all their rows use temperature 1.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Triton port of the fused GDN MTP decode kernel
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Overview

GDN layers with the flat qkvz layout (Qwen3.5 family) fall back to the unfused speculative-decode path on ROCm because `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` (#51674) only builds for CUDA. This adds a Triton port with the same signature and uses it on ROCm: a state-update kernel tiled over the value dimension like `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` (tile size chosen from the grid size) plus a small gated-RMSNorm epilogue. It covers every model built on `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` with the flat layout: the Qwen3.5 family, Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (table below). Qwen3-Next (interleaved layout) stays ineligible, as on CUDA.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, MTP k=3, 1x MI350X, one request at a time: decode 2.39 -> 2.08 ms/token (-13%), E2E 544 -> 488 ms (-10%), on vLLM main (nightly `77154ca`) with aiter main. The first version of this PR (one program per value head, no V tiling) gave 2.19 ms/token in the same side-by-side run.
- Per decode step on MI350X: copy/fill/cat kernels 1.56 -> 0.31 ms, kernel launches 1008 -> 768, GPU kernel time 7.74 -> 6.71 ms.
- Faster at higher concurrency too: per-step time (median ITL) -12% at 1, -6% at 8 and -6% at 32 concurrent requests, output throughput +14% / +16% / +10% (`vllm bench serve`, 2K/256).
- Numerics match the unfused path: the existing MTP kernel test, parametrized over CUDA op / Triton port, passes for the Triton port on MI350X and MI300X (22/22 each); states are bit-identical to the first version at every tile size, and outputs are too or differ only in the rounding of the norm's sum; MTP acceptance unchanged (2.85-2.87 accepted tokens per step).
- Accuracy unchanged: GPQA Diamond 0.821 (main) vs 0.826 (this PR), needle-in-a-haystack 100% for both at 4K-64K tokens.
- Long context (64K in / 1K out): decode step (median ITL) -12% / -6% / -3% at 1 / 8 / 32 concurrent requests; prefill unchanged.
- MI300X (gfx942): per call, 49-60% faster than the unfused path at 1 request and 25-44% at 32 (table below).
- GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run variation (base 0.854-0.861 over 4 runs, this PR 0.848-0.862 over 3 runs), above the 0.84 threshold in `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DEP2.yaml`.
- CUDA unchanged: the CUDA op is still used wherever it is built.

## Validation

Kernel test (MI350X and MI300X, ROCm 7.2.3; the CUDA-op cases skip because the op is not built on ROCm):

```
pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -k mtp
22 passed, 22 skipped
```

## Details

Models that take the fused path on ROCm with this change (eligibility is unchanged from the CUDA op: flat qkvz layout, K = V = 128, value/key head ratio 1/2/3/4/8, BF16 activations, at most 8 tokens per verify):

| Model | vLLM model code | GDN K/V heads (ratio) | GDN layers | Validated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/64 (4) | 45 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/64 (4) | 36 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/32 (2) | 30 | end to end (this PR) |
| Qwen3.5-27B / 9B / 2B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/48 (3) / 16/32 (2) / 16/16 (1) | 48 / 24 / 18 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.8-27B | `qwen3_5.py` (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) | 16/48 (3) | 48 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (incl. FP8) | `vllm/models/qwen4_exp` (same GDN layer, flat layout) | 16/48 (3) | 36 | kernel test |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | `qwen3_next.py` (interleaved layout) | 16/32 (2) | - | not eligible (unchanged) |


- **Root cause.** On ROCm the layer logs `Falling back to the Triton GDN spec decode path: torch.ops._C.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp is not built`. The AITER fused GDN path only covers non-speculative decode, so every GDN layer's verify step runs ~8 small kernels around the recurrent kernel: contiguous copies of `a`/`b`, three copies plus a `cat` to unpack q/k/v, a zero-fill, an output copy, and the gated RMSNorm.
- **Kernels.** Two launches. The update kernel runs one program per (request, value head, tile of the value dimension). It reads q/k/v and `a`/`b` in place from the projections and runs the gated delta-rule update over the request's tokens with the same state reads and writes as `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`: start from the state at the last accepted token, store the state after every token, slot index <= 0 means no state. Each tile writes its rows of the output and their sum of squares per token. The epilogue, one program per (request, value head, token), adds the partial sums and applies the gated RMSNorm, the only step that needs the whole value dimension, then writes the `out_proj` input. Recurrent state layout is `[slot, HV, V, K]`, BF16 or FP32.
- **Tile size.** 32 rows per program while there are fewer (request, value head) pairs than CUs, 64 up to 4x the CUs, else one tile per value head. A sweep of 32/64/128 rows on MI300X and MI350X (both head shapes, both state dtypes, 1-32 requests) put this rule within 8% of the best tile size everywhere; a fixed 32 was up to 36% slower at 16-32 requests on MI300X.
- **Wiring.** Same keyword signature as the CUDA op; the layer picks the Triton port on ROCm. `forward_hip` routes speculative-decode configs to the packed fused-norm path (`forward_cuda`); non-speculative ROCm decode keeps the AITER path. Opt out with the existing `VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton`.
- **Per call.** Qwen3.5-35B-A3B shape (16/32 K/V heads), 4 tokens per request, CUDA-graph replay, current ROCm nightly image; "first version" is this PR before the review (one program per value head):

  | GPU | State | Requests | unfused | first version | this PR |

  | MI350X | FP32 | 1 | 30.0 us | 18.7 us | 11.5 us |
  | MI350X | FP32 | 8 | 46.7 us | 26.8 us | 21.8 us |
  | MI350X | FP32 | 32 | 91.4 us | 71.9 us | 64.3 us |
  | MI350X | BF16 | 1 | 28.3 us | 12.5 us | 10.2 us |
  | MI350X | BF16 | 32 | 68.1 us | 36.5 us | 39.6 us |
  | MI300X | FP32 | 1 | 30.2 us | 21.7 us | 13.3 us |
  | MI300X | FP32 | 8 | 56.7 us | 38.5 us | 33.3 us |
  | MI300X | FP32 | 32 | 145.7 us | 96.8 us | 88.8 us |
  | MI300X | BF16 | 1 | 28.5 us | 16.3 us | 11.3 us |
  | MI300X | BF16 | 32 | 117.0 us | 66.5 us | 65.2 us |

  With FP32 state, the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 default (`mamba_ssm_dtype: float32`), this PR is faster than the first version at every batch size on both GPUs. With BF16 state at 32 requests on MI350X it is 8-9% slower than the first version (one tile per head plus the epilogue launch), still well ahead of the unfused path. The 16/48 head shape behaves the same way.
- **Coverage.** End to end this was run on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B only. The other models in the table are covered by the kernel test, which runs every eligible head ratio (1/2/3/4/8) at TP 1-16, but were not run end to end.
- **CI.** The parametrized test runs the Triton port on any GPU (NVIDIA too), so existing CUDA CI covers its numerics; AMD CI covers the ROCm path where it runs `tests/kernels/fla`.
- **Related open PRs (not duplicates).**
  - #61675 adds an opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_QWEN_MTP_GDN`), shape-specialized ROCm kernel that also fuses the conv. It accepts only 16/48 K/V heads (Qwen3.8-27B), TP=1 and verify widths up to 4, and raises for any other shape, including Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (16/32). This PR makes the default ROCm path fused under the same contract and eligibility as the upstream CUDA op (head ratios 1/2/3/4/8, any TP, up to 8 tokens). The two can coexist, with #61675 taking over when it is enabled.
  - #61434 defers state stores inside the unfused Triton spec-decode kernel (FP32 state, `mamba_cache_mode="none"`). On ROCm this PR replaces that path whenever the fused path is eligible; the deferred-store idea could be applied to this kernel in a follow-up.
  - #59366 adds a separate CUDA replay op for RecoverSSM and leaves the op ported here unchanged.
  - #60833 / #61325 (Qwen3.8 mono decode on MI355X) run vLLM's GDN core for verify steps, so this change applies there too.
- **Provenance.** The first version of the kernel was written and validated in Meta's internal vLLM fork; the V tiling was added in this PR after review.
