commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Skip drafting in steps where no request can use the drafts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Continues #48244 by @njhill (co-author). In steps where no scheduled request can use the
drafts proposed after the step, the speculator now proposes with K=0 instead of
drafting. Such requests are non-final prefill chunks and requests sure to reach
`max_tokens`. This covers every request on a P/D prefill instance, which runs with
`max_tokens=1`.

Related: #39266 (draft) skips EAGLE drafting on MRV2 for P/D prefill instances and
non-final chunks; this PR decides in the scheduler and also covers requests about to
finish, DFlash and DP. #53426 makes the K=0 draft sync forward optional; this PR keeps
that forward.

## Claims

- On Model Runner V2, when no scheduled request on any DP rank can use the drafts, the
  speculator runs with `num_speculative_tokens=0`:
  - EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP still run the draft prefill pass, which keeps the drafter's KV cache
    in sync, but skip draft sampling and the draft decode steps.
  - DFlash stores the context K/V and skips the query pass. DSpark, DFlash2 and
    LiLiCorr share this code.
- The drafter's prefill pass still runs, so the gain is modest. Prefill-only throughput
  (Qwen3-8B, 64 x 16,384-token prompts, 1 output token, one GB300 GPU) improves by
  **+1.9% with EAGLE3** and **+7.3% with DFlash** at `max_num_batched_tokens=512`, and by
  +1.4% and +2.7% at 2048. On a 1P1D prefill instance every step proposes with K=0,
  and prefill throughput improves by +2.1% (EAGLE3) and +3.4% (DFlash) at 512, and by
  +0.6% and +1.9% at 2048.
- Outputs and acceptance do not change. With batch-invariant kernels, outputs and every
  spec-decode counter are identical to `main`.

## Validation

Qwen3-8B with `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` (K=3) and `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (K=16),
`--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN`, GB300. Baseline is `main` at `532a7d19d2`, the base of
this PR; every run below used the rebased commit.

An earlier version of this description reported +9.0% (EAGLE3) and +3.4% (DFlash) at 512.
Those runs were CPU-starved (the benchmark processes were confined to one CPU core),
which inflated host-side costs. The numbers below replace them.

**Prefill-only throughput** (total tokens/s; mean of 3 reps on one engine after a warm-up
pass). The workload matches `vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random
--random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 64 --max-model-len 20480`.
main and this PR ran at the same time on two GPUs of one node, then swapped GPUs. The
table shows the GPU whose reps stayed within 1%; on the other GPU, reps of both builds
varied by up to 30%. With the PR, every proposal in these runs used K=0.

| Method | `max_num_batched_tokens` | main | this PR | Delta | Step time saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | 2048 | 72,100 | 73,144 | +1.4% | 0.4 ms |
| EAGLE3 | 512 | 33,834 | 34,473 | **+1.9%** | 0.3 ms |
| DFlash | 2048 | 72,569 | 74,508 | +2.7% | 0.7 ms |
| DFlash | 512 | 32,367 | 34,730 | **+7.3%** | 1.1 ms |

The skipped work is draft sampling and the draft decode steps (EAGLE3), or the query pass
(DFlash). Host time spent in `propose()` at 512 drops from 1.41 to 0.98 ms per step for
EAGLE3 and from 1.05 to 0.92 ms for DFlash; the rest of the saving is GPU time. The
drafter's prefill pass still runs: it writes the draft KV cache that later steps, and on
a P/D decode instance the transferred KV, depend on.

**1P1D prefill throughput.** P and D each on one GPU with `NixlConnector`, the same
drafter on both, P at the given `max_num_batched_tokens`. Through the toy proxy, 3
phases of 128 random 8,192-token prompts at concurrency 32 (`max_tokens=8`). P's waiting
queue was non-empty in at least 89% of samples. main and this PR ran side by side on the
node's two GPU pairs, then swapped; tokens/s and deltas are means over both placements.

| Method | P `max_num_batched_tokens` | main | this PR | Delta | P proposals with K=0 (PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | 2048 | 56,809 | 57,213 | +0.6% | 3,072 / 3,072 |
| EAGLE3 | 512 | 28,447 | 29,043 | **+2.1%** | 12,288 / 12,288 |
| DFlash | 2048 | 56,950 | 57,883 | +1.9% | 3,072 / 3,072 |
| DFlash | 512 | 28,527 | 29,524 | **+3.4%** | 12,288 / 12,288 |

**Equivalence** (offline, greedy). There are 80 requests: 24 long prompts chunked at 512
tokens with `max_tokens` 1, 2 or 64, run alone and then mixed with 32 short decode
requests.

| Method | Mode | Outputs equal | Spec-decode counters | Proposals with K=0 (PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | 80/80 | identical (3,349 drafts, 1,775 accepted) | 19 |
| DFlash | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | 80/80 | identical (2,244 drafts, 2,953 accepted) | 18 |

Without batch invariance, two runs of `main` already differ on 23/80 EAGLE3 outputs, and
main vs this PR differ on 31/80. DFlash is deterministic across runs of `main`, but main
vs this PR differ on 31/80: in a K=0 step DFlash stores all context K/V in one eager
pass instead of partly inside the FULL graph, so rounding can differ, and acceptance then
changes batch shapes.

**Existing e2e tests** give the same results on both:

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/test_eagle_correctness.py -k "medium and qwen3_eagle3 and not transformers"` | GSM8K 0.886, pass | GSM8K 0.886, pass |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py` (MRV2 reference acceptance) | MT-Bench 4.07, HumanEval 6.42, GSM8K 6.42 | same |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py::test_dflash_correctness[qwen3-mrv2]` | GSM8K 0.884, AL 4.12 | same |

**Serving equivalence.** 1P1D with `NixlConnector` used EAGLE3 K=3 on both sides and CUDA
graphs on. DP=2 used EAGLE3 K=3. Requests were sent one at a time.

| Setup | Outputs equal | Decode-side acceptance length |
|---|---|---|
| 1P1D | 40/40 | identical (1.521, 1.598) |
| DP=2 | 40/40 | identical (1.539, 1.597) |

There were no hangs with DP ranks voting to skip.

**Unit tests.** `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`,
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py` and
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py` pass (281 tests), except two
pre-existing PP scheduler tests that fail the same way on `main`.

## Details

- **Scheduler.** It sets `SchedulerOutput.skip_drafts` when no scheduled request can use
  the step's drafts, on the V2 runner and for drafters that reserve lookahead slots.
  `_drafts_unused` counts only the output tokens a request is sure to have, assuming
  every draft is rejected, so it never skips drafts a later step could verify.
- **DP.** The flag is ANDed across ranks in the batch-descriptor all-reduce that already
  runs, giving `DPSyncState.skip_drafts`. The runner then proposes with K=0. A rank
  running a dummy batch votes no, so an idle DP rank disables the skip for that step.
- **Changes from #48244:**
  - The per-request lookahead-slot skip is dropped. For a non-final chunk, the lookahead
    slots are the next chunk's first positions, which are allocated one step later
    anyway. For a finishing request it saves at most about one block for one step.
    Keeping it safely means masking every draft KV write, including inside captured
    FULL draft-decode graphs; the fused decode path is the default on FlashAttention,
    FlashInfer and Triton, and its captured graphs compute their own slot mappings.
  - Skipping reuses the existing `num_speculative_tokens == 0` path, which already skips
    the AR draft decode steps, instead of a separate flag in each speculator.
    `skip_sample` and the DFlash early return also apply to K=0 from dynamic speculative
    decoding.
  - The scheduler reports one flag instead of a set of request ids.
- **Not covered.** Multi-module MTP and the draft-model speculator ignore K, so they
  still draft in these steps and the drafts go unused, as before. N-gram reserves no
  lookahead slots, so the flag is never set for it. MTP, DSpark, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr
  share the changed code but were not run; all validation used Qwen3-8B. MRV1 is
  unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Throughput script (one engine, warm-up then timed reps)</summary>

```python
llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B", speculative_config=spec, max_model_len=20480,
          max_num_batched_tokens=mbt, enable_prefix_caching=False, seed=42,
          attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN")
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
prompts = lambda n: [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=r.tolist())
                     for r in rng.integers(1000, 100000, size=(n, 16384))]
params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True)
llm.generate(prompts(8), params)
for _ in range(3):
    batch = prompts(64)
    t = time.perf_counter(); llm.generate(batch, params)
    print(64 * 16385 / (time.perf_counter() - t))
```
</details>

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Part of #57997. `translate_error_response()` now maps vLLM's internal error types to Anthropic's documented `error.type` vocabulary (e.g. `not_found_error`, `invalid_request_error`, `api_error`) instead of copying names like `NotFoundError`.

The validation-envelope half of #57997 is already covered by open PR #58023, so this PR intentionally does not touch that path.

## Claims

- Unknown model on `/v1/messages` returns `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"not_found_error",...}}` while keeping HTTP 404.
- Other statuses map to Anthropic types: 400/422 -> `invalid_request_error`, 401 -> `authentication_error`, 403 -> `permission_error`, 404 -> `not_found_error`, 413 -> `request_too_large`, 429 -> `rate_limit_error`, 5xx -> `api_error`, 529 -> `overloaded_error`.
- HTTP status code and message are preserved.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU-only):

```text
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_error_type_mapping.py -q
12 passed
```

End-to-end on `main` at `3f1b04e045` with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` on an RTX 2080 Ti (Triton attention backend); the branch is rebased onto `072c0886`:

Before:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"NotFoundError","message":"The model `does-not-exist` does not exist. Valid aliases: Qwen3.5-4B."}}
HTTP 404
```

After:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"not_found_error","message":"The model `does-not-exist` does not exist. Valid aliases: Qwen3.5-4B."}}
HTTP 404
```

Control: the same validation error on `/v1/messages` still uses the existing OpenAI-shaped envelope (`HTTP 400`), confirming this PR only changes `error.type` translation.

## Details

Root cause: `translate_error_response()` copied `ErrorResponse.error.type` verbatim. vLLM builds that field from internal exception class names (`NotFoundError`, `BadRequestError`, `InternalServerError`, ...), but Anthropic SDKs dispatch on the snake_case values defined by the Anthropic API.

Approach: derive the Anthropic type from the HTTP status code, which `create_error_response()` already sets consistently, and fall back to `api_error` for 5xx / `invalid_request_error` for other 4xx. This also normalizes `GracefulHTTPError`, whose type is currently an HTTP phrase (e.g. `"Bad Request"`).

Tradeoff: status-based mapping is intentionally coarse. Anthropic's public API distinguishes `request_too_large` (413) and `overloaded_error` (529), which the mapping handles explicitly. Other 4xx statuses collapse to `invalid_request_error`, matching Anthropic's client-facing behavior.

## Not duplicating existing work

- #58023 covers the validation-envelope half (`RequestValidationError` handling) and is still open; this PR does not modify it.
- #43380 adds a `VLLMValidationError -> invalid_request_error` branch at 400 for the two endpoints; this PR generalizes the mapping in `translate_error_response()` for all statuses, including 404/429/5xx.
- #59968 fixes authentication-middleware envelopes; that path does not go through `translate_error_response()`.

Developed with AI assistance (Codex). The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and reproduced the fix end-to-end with a real model server.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Add XPress speculative decoding method
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Adds **XPress**, a causal refiner for block-diffusion drafters, as a V1 speculative decoding method alongside DFlash and DSpark. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02438

A block-diffusion drafter such as DFlash proposes a whole block in one forward pass, which makes drafting cheap, and decodes it from per-position marginals, which makes it inaccurate: token *k* is drawn without seeing what the drafter chose at *k-1*. The target verifies conditionally, so blocks that are individually plausible but jointly improbable are rejected early, capping acceptance length. 


## Design

XPress adds a small head that reads the drafter's per-position hidden state, a block-global summary and the previous token, fuses them into a rank-256 bottleneck, mixes across the block with a lower-triangular (causal) mixer, and reads back out as a bias on the base logits. Everything except the two vocabulary projections lives in the bottleneck (~80M params, 96% of
which are those two matrices).

Because the mixer is true causal rather than local smooth, the block is resolved by **Jacobi iteration** rather than a left-to right loop: the same call runs K times, each pass re-feeding the previous pass's argmax, so the serial depth is a constant K instead of the block size. Both stages are fixed-shape and loop-free, so the whole draft step is CUDA-graph capturable, which is what makes K passes cheap: they cost K matmuls, not K kernel launches. Two Triton kernels keep a pass at three launches (`xpress_latent_pass`, and a fused add+argmax that writes straight into the block buffer so the [N, B, V] sum is never materialized).

`XPressSpeculator` subclasses `DFlashSpeculator` and overrides only draft generation; attention, KV cache setup and weight sharing are inherited unchanged. Existing files gain **39 lines** of method registration; everything else is new files.

## Test Plan

```bash
# e2e (80GB GPU; public Qwen3-8B + XPress checkpoint pair): full GSM8K at temperature 0,
# accuracy and acceptance metrics against reference values -- same protocol as the
# DFlash and DSpark tests in acceptance_rates/
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py -s
```

The e2e test guards GSM8K accuracy and acceptance rate and length against references, with an upper bound on acceptance length. Note that acceptance length moves by about 0.5% with anything that changes the vLLM config hash, because the hash keys torch.compile's cache and autotuning then picks different kernels, shifting the floating-point reduction order so that near-tie draft tokens flip. Under `enforce_eager=True` the paths are identical. 

<details><summary>Serving and benchmark commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15}'

# optional: narrow each Jacobi pass to the drafter's top-C candidates
# (default 512; 0 scores the full vocabulary)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative_config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15,"xpress_topc":256}'
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept and echo prompt-cache and safety_identifier fields in the Responses API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62855. `/v1/responses` now accepts `safety_identifier`, `prompt_cache_retention` and `prompt_cache_options` as typed fields and echoes them, together with `prompt_cache_key` (#32824), on the response object, as OpenAI does.

## Claims

- The three fields are declared on `ResponsesRequest`, so they are validated. Before this change they were untyped extras
- `ResponsesResponse` echoes all four through `from_request`, which covers non-streaming, streaming (`response.created` …) and background responses
- `prompt_cache_retention` accepts `"in-memory"` (older `openai` SDKs), `"in_memory"` (current SDKs) and `"24h"`. Any other value returns 400
- No change for requests that don't send these fields; they echo as `null`

## Validation

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py`: each field is echoed, an omitted field is `None`, invalid retention or `ttl` is rejected, and `response.created` carries the fields. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.

## Details

- Root cause: #32824 declared `prompt_cache_key` on the request but not on the response; the other three fields were never declared
- `PromptCacheOptions` is defined locally because the minimum supported `openai` (2.25) doesn't have it
- No length limit on `safety_identifier`. vLLM doesn't use the value, and a limit would turn requests that succeed today into 400s
- vLLM still doesn't act on these fields; the field descriptions say so

Claude Code used to validate the tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix FA4 FP8 descale strides for singleton KV heads
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a FlashAttention 4 FP8 KV-cache crash when a per-tensor Q/K/V scale is expanded to a descale tensor with a non-unit head stride:

```text
Expected strides[leading_dim] == 1, but got 0
```

This was encountered in a Nemotron-H deployment with two total KV heads and TP=2 on B200 (vLLM 0.29.0). Each rank has one KV head. At batch size 1, `scalar.expand(1, 1)` has strides `(0, 0)` but PyTorch considers it contiguous, so `.contiguous()` can leave the incompatible stride unchanged. FA4 converts descales to CuTe tensors with `leading_dim=1`.

Materialize only 2-D FA4 descales whose head stride is not one using `clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)`. Preserve compatible inputs and the existing non-FP8 behavior. This copies the small scale tensors, not the KV cache.

## Test Plan

Add a CPU regression suite that calls the production `flash_attn_varlen_func` and replaces only the downstream CuTe kernel entry point. It verifies the forwarded descale layout, values, and reuse of compatible inputs across:

- batch sizes 1 and 3;
- one and two local KV heads;
- scalar-expanded, per-head-expanded, and absent descales;
- FP8 e4m3, FP8 e5m2, and BF16 inputs.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn_interface.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn_interface.py
```

The sibling kernel suite requires the CUDA package initializer. This test loads the Python wrapper directly so it can also run on a CPU-only machine. The existing attention-kernel CI glob includes the new file.

commits.pr_title: [bug-fix] Fix KV block leak with fault tolerance enabled in P/D disaggregation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Extend the fault tolerance (FT) framework (#44428) to prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregated deployments. When KV transfer is enabled, a worker failure currently causes two problems:

1. **KV transfer progress loss.** When `_model_forward` raises, the exception path discards the `kv_connector_output`, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` for in-flight transfers are lost. After `retry` recovery, the scheduler's KV transfer bookkeeping no longer matches the actual connector state, and requests can hang or leak KV blocks.

2. **Response queue residue.** In the executor's `get_response`, the first `FAILURE` response raises immediately, without dequeuing the remaining workers' responses. The stale responses left in the MQs are then consumed by the *next* RPC call, corrupting subsequent steps.

Key design:

- **Preserve KV state on failure**: a failed worker's `kv_connector_output` is extracted before the exception is shipped, carried via a new `ExceptionWithKVConnectorOutput` / `ResponseStatus.FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` status, and deferred into the executor's `KVOutputAggregator`
- **Drain-then-raise**: `get_response` always dequeues **all** workers' responses before raising (this covers all collective RPCs, not just `execute_model`), so no residue is left in the response queues
- **Defer-and-replay**: `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` stashes salvaged outputs; they are replayed through the normal `aggregate()` loop at the next successful step, so pending transfers are correctly reported without any special-case merging logic. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped (see Details)
- **Consume, don't drop**: on recovery, `EngineCoreSentinel` drains the batch queue and consumes each future's `kv_connector_output` (worker-side connectors use get-and-clear semantics) instead of clearing the queue wholesale
- **No new control flow**: everything rides the existing response MQ, batch queue, and `KVOutputAggregator` mechanisms

### Details

1. **Async output extraction.** `get_kv_connector_output()` is added to `AsyncModelRunnerOutput` and its implementations (v1 GPU runner, v2 `AsyncOutput` / `AsyncPoolingOutput`). In `WorkerProc.enqueue_output`, when `get_output()` raises, the pending `kv_connector_output` is extracted and shipped to the executor as `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`.

2. **Drain-then-raise in the executor.** In `get_response`, a `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT` no longer raises immediately. All workers' responses are dequeued; KV connector outputs (explicit or embedded in successful responses) are stashed via `KVOutputAggregator.ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs`, and only then is the error raised. Stale exception responses from other ranks are dropped. When FT is disabled or the executor has already failed, the original raise-immediately behavior is preserved.

3. **Defer-and-replay in the aggregator.** Salvaged outputs are stashed by `ft_defer_kv_connector_outputs` and replayed through the normal aggregation loop at the next successful `aggregate()` call, so `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` / `failed_recving` / `invalid_block_ids` and worker metadata are preserved exactly as if they had arrived late. Salvaged `kv_cache_events` are dropped at stash time: a dropped event only costs a cache miss until its blocks are stored again, while replaying them could perturb the surviving workers' event quorum (e.g. overshooting LMCache's `count == num_workers` exact-match threshold). `aggregate()` itself is unchanged.

4. **Batch queue drain on recovery.** `EngineCoreSentinel` now drains the batch queue instead of `clear()`ing it: each pending future's `kv_connector_output` is consumed and applied via `scheduler.update_from_output(SchedulerOutput.make_empty(), ModelRunnerOutput.with_kv_conn_output_only(...))` (KV transfer state only -- the rest of the model output is not applied to avoid corrupting scheduler state mid-recovery).

## Test Plan

Unit tests added in this PR:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
    tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py \
    tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_engine_core_sentinel.py -v
```

- `test_output_aggregator.py`: replay of salvaged transfer fields, completion of recv votes, and salvaged event votes never entering the quorum (LMCache exact-match and Mooncake `>=` semantics, including late-live-vote cases)
- `test_executor.py`: drain-then-raise behavior of `get_response` under `FAILURE` / `FAILURE_WITH_KV_OUTPUT`
- `test_engine_core_sentinel.py`: batch queue drain surfaces `kv_connector_output` and drops failed futures

CI wiring: `.buildkite/test_areas/fault_tolerance.yaml` now runs the sentinel test in the FT pipeline, and `source_file_dependencies` covers `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/` and `vllm/v1/executor/` so aggregator/executor-only changes trigger it.

Manual verification:

**Model**: Qwen3-30B-A3B
**Configuration**: 1 prefill (kv_producer) + 1 decode (kv_consumer), MooncakeConnector, fault tolerance enabled

### Launching the cluster

Each instance runs as a separate `vllm serve` process.

**Prefill instance (producer)** -- GPU 0, port 8010:

```bash
VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT=8998 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8010 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Decode instance (consumer)** -- GPU 1, port 8020:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
vllm serve <MODEL> \
    --port 8020 \
    --kv-transfer-config \
    '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}' \
    --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30 \
    --enable-fault-tolerance \
    --fault-tolerance-config '{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 500}'
```

**Proxy** (routes requests between P and D instances):

```bash
python3 examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
    --prefill http://0.0.0.0:8010 8998 \
    --decode http://0.0.0.0:8020 \
    --port 8000
```

### Simulating faults

To simulate a device-side failure on the decode instance, inject a `RuntimeError` in the forward path, raising at a chosen step on the target rank:

```python
# Fault injection: raise at specific steps
if step_count in [250, 5000]:
    raise RuntimeError("FAULT INJECTION: exception in forward path")
```

### Sending inference requests

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model": "<MODEL>", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 128}'
```

### Querying FT status and issuing recovery

```bash
# Query engine status (one per instance port):
curl -s http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/status
curl -s http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/status

# Issue retry to both instances after both become unhealthy:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8010/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8020/fault_tolerance/apply \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"instruction": "retry", "params": {"timeout": 120}}'
```

## Overview

Part of #48227 (Step 5). Switches the remaining client-input `ValueError`s in `vllm/renderers/base.py` to `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter` set. The file already raises `VLLMValidationError` for out-of-vocabulary token ids and `truncate_prompt_tokens`; these seven sites were the leftovers.

## Claims

- Seven raise sites in `BaseRenderer` now raise `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter` set. The message strings are unchanged.
- HTTP: these were already 400 through the raw-`ValueError` fallback in `create_error_response`. They now go through the `VLLMValidationError` branch, so `param` is filled instead of `null`. Like every `VLLMValidationError`, the message gets a ` (parameter=...)` suffix.
- The deprecated raw-prompt path of `AsyncLLM.generate()` (`InputProcessor.process_inputs` -> `render_cmpl`) only re-raises `VLLMClientError` since Step 3. These checks used to be wrapped into `EngineGenerateError` there. Now they surface as validation errors.

## Validation

Tests (CPU only, no model weights). No new tests. The existing checks that expected `ValueError` now expect `VLLMValidationError`:

- `tests/renderers/test_completions.py`: `test_empty_input`.
- `tests/renderers/test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py`: `test_multi_modal_uuids_length_mismatch_raises` (both cases) and `test_multi_modal_uuids_missing_modal
ity_raises`.

Commands (WSL Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12, CPU torch, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):

```bash
pytest -q tests/renderers/test_completions.py                # 43 passed
pytest -q tests/renderers/test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py  # 13 passed
pytest -q tests/renderers                                    # 642 passed, 3 failed (all environmental: 2 gated HF repos, 1 model-weight download blocked loc
ally; the same 3 fail on main)
pre-commit run --files tests/renderers/test_completions.py tests/renderers/test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py  # all hooks passed
```

Error body for `POST /v1/completions` with `{"prompt": []}`, as built by `create_error_response` from the exception each version raises:

```json
// before
{"error": {"message": "You must pass at least one prompt", "type": "BadRequestError", "param": null, "code": 400}}
// after
{"error": {"message": "You must pass at least one prompt (parameter=prompt)", "type": "BadRequestError", "param": "prompt", "code": 400}}
```


## Details

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches these sites, and no comment on #48227 claims `vllm/renderers/`. The latest claim there (TylerMa-debugg, 2026-10-04) is the pooling entrypoints only. Searched open PRs for `VLLMValidationError renderers`, `multi_modal_uuids VLLMValidationError`, `prompt_embeds VLLMValidationError` and `48227`, and found nothing.

**Sites changed:**

| Site | Check | `parameter` | Reached from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render_prompts`, `render_prompts_async` | empty prompt list | `prompt` | `/v1/completions` with `"prompt": []` (the `CompletionRequest` validator only treats `None`/`""` as empty); `LLM.generate([])` |
| `_validate_mm_uuids` (3 raises) | uuid missing for an empty modality or item; uuid list length differs from data | `multi_modal_uuids` | Per-item case: a chat `image_embeds: null` part with no `uuid` (with `--enable-mm-embeds`), or `/inference/v1/generate` `content_parts` with neither `url` nor `uuid`. All three: prompts passing `multi_modal_data`/`multi_modal_uuids` (`LLM.generate`, raw `AsyncLLM` prompts) |
| `_process_embeds` (2 raises) | `--enable-prompt-embeds` not set; tensor not 2D | `prompt_embeds` | Raw-tensor `EmbedsPrompt` from `LLM.generate` or `AsyncLLM`. HTTP `prompt_embeds` already fails the same checks earlier in `safe_load_prompt_embeds`, which uses `parameter="prompt_embeds"`, so both paths now match |

`multi_modal_uuids` names the field the message already refers to. Chat clients set `uuid` per content part, but `BaseRenderer` doesn't know which endpoint it is serving, so it uses the prompt-level name.

**Left unchanged:**

- `get_tokenizer` ("Tokenizer not available when `skip_tokenizer_init=True`") and `get_mm_processor` ("Multi-modal processor not available for text-only models"): these are server-configuration checks, so they need their own classification and are not request validation.
- The `TypeError`s in `_tokenize_singleton_prompt{,_async}`: these are prompt-type invariants that run after parsing.
- The `RuntimeError`s (no decoder start token, detokenizing embeddings): these are internal.

**Compatibility.** `VLLMValidationError` no longer subclasses `ValueError` (Step 1). Offline code that catches `ValueError` around these errors needs `VLLMValidationError` instead. This is the same trade-off #53432 made for `LLM.generate` input checks. I found no `except ValueError` in `vllm/` that wraps these call paths. Online, they reach the global `VLLMError` handler.

commits.pr_title: [Feature] [Frontend] [Reasoning] Support Prompt Embeds inputs for reasoning traces
commits.pr_body:
## Overview



Allow assistant messages in `/v1/chat/completions` to supply a single `prompt_embeds` part as `reasoning`, using the existing support for prompt embeddings in message content.

I found no existing relevant issues and PRs that are currently open. This follows-up to a whole slew of work done in the past enabling prompt embeds support for `/v1/chat/completions` request.

## Claims



- Accepts `reasoning` as text or a prompt embedding part, including through the legacy `reasoning_content` alias.
- Reuses existing embedding decoding, validation, and rendering, preserving embedding order when both reasoning and content contain embeddings.
- Prevents forwarded `kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids` from bypassing reasoning embedding processing.


## Validation



Local validation during development:

| Coverage | Result |
|---|---|
| Renderer prompt embedding and assistant suites | 110 passed |
| Focused rendering, alias, validation, and token reuse checks | 31 passed |
| Final standalone KV transfer regression test | 1 passed |
| Full prompt embedding chat completion suite | 12 passed |

The serving suite used OPT-125M with BF16 on an RTX A6000. Equivalent text and token embeddings produced identical greedy output and prompt token counts. 

Relevant suites can be reproduced with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_assistant.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_chat_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_ignored_with_reasoning_embeds -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion_with_prompt_embeds.py -q
```

The tests I touched run locally. I cannot run the entire test suite locally, unfortunately, and have to rely on CI.

### Manual validation

I also have a script to manually validate that prompt embedding-encoded inputs are passed to the engine when provided.

It asks the model to repeat back a secret code, but the secret code is only provided in the reasoning trace of a previous message. We expect the answer to be correct and identical regardless of whether the reasoning traces are passed in as prompt embeddings or plain text.

<details>
<summary> Script </summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""vLLM OpenAI-Compatible Client with Prompt Embeddings.

Adapted from the official vLLM docs. 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/features/prompt_embed/prompt_embed_inference_with_openai_client.py

This adapted version uses Qwen 3.5, which does respect reasoning (albeit only in the current turn) in its chat
template. It also only exercises the /v1/chat/completions path, as that is the only path that supports reasoning
with prompt embeds.

It runs chat completions with prompt embeddings inputs. The first time, the entire conversation, including reasoning traces, is encoded into prompt embeds.
The second time, the reasoning traces are left as plaintext.

This shows that outputs are identical with reasoning being prompt embeddings or plaintext. 

Furthermore, the prompt can only be answered correctly if the model sees the reasoning traces (which contain the secret code).
"""

import transformers
from openai import OpenAI

from vllm.utils.serial_utils import tensor2base64

def encode(tokenizer: transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase, embedding_layer, text: str) -> str:
    token_ids = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False).input_ids
    prompt_embeds = embedding_layer(token_ids).squeeze(0)
    return tensor2base64(prompt_embeds)

def encode_message(msg: dict, tokenizer, embedding_layer, encode_reasoning:bool) -> dict:
    if msg.get("role") == "tool":
        return msg
    encoded_msg = {
        "role": msg['role'],
        "content": msg['content']
    }
    if "reasoning" in msg:
        encoded_msg['reasoning'] = {
            "type": "prompt_embeds",
            "data": encode(tokenizer, embedding_layer, msg['reasoning']),
        } if encode_reasoning else msg['reasoning']
    if "tool_calls" in msg:
        encoded_msg['tool_calls'] = msg["tool_calls"]

    return encoded_msg


def run_chat_completion_prompt_embeds(
    client: OpenAI,
    model_name: str,
    tokenizer: transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase,
    embedding_layer,
    messages: list[dict],
    encode_reasoning: bool,
) -> None:
    """Run a Chat Completions API request using prompt_embeds content parts."""
    api_messages = [
        encode_message(message, tokenizer, embedding_layer, encode_reasoning) for message in messages
    ]

    chat_completion = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=model_name,
        max_tokens=1024,
        temperature=0.0,
        messages=api_messages,
    )

    print("-" * 30)
    print("Chat Completions API")
    print(f"Encoding reasoning traces to prompt embeds: {encode_reasoning}")
    print("-" * 30)
    print(chat_completion.choices[0].message.content)
    print("-" * 30)



def main() -> None:
    client = OpenAI(
        api_key="EMPTY",
        base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    )

    model_name = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B"

    tokenizer = transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    transformers_model = transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)
    embedding_layer = transformers_model.get_input_embeddings()

    messages_with_reasoning  = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "What was the secret code I established?",
    },
    {
        "role": "assistant",
        "reasoning": (
            "The secret code is A1dhgl3ihz. "
            "I must remember it after checking the tool."
        ),
        "content": "",
        "tool_calls": [
            {
                "id": "call_1",
                "type": "function",
                "function": {
                    "name": "check_status",
                    "arguments": "{}",
                },
            }
        ],
    },
    {
        "role": "tool",
        "tool_call_id": "call_1",
        "name": "check_status",
        "content": "Status: OK",
    },
]
    run_chat_completion_prompt_embeds(
            client, model_name, tokenizer, embedding_layer, messages_with_reasoning, encode_reasoning=True
        )
    run_chat_completion_prompt_embeds(
            client, model_name, tokenizer, embedding_layer, messages_with_reasoning, encode_reasoning=False
        )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
</details>

```
------------------------------
Chat Completions API
Encoding reasoning traces to prompt embeds: True
The secret code I established is **A1dhgl3ihz**.
------------------------------
------------------------------
Chat Completions API
Encoding reasoning traces to prompt embeds: False
The secret code I established is **A1dhgl3ihz**.
------------------------------
```

## Details




Prompt embeddings let callers supply representations in the model’s continuous input space. Extending this capability to reasoning inputs supports experimentation with richer reasoning representations, motivated by work such as [Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06769) and [Hybrid Reasoning Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18861). 

It also makes reasoning inputs available to the same applications as content embeddings: prompt compression, custom encoders, and Protopia’s [Stained Glass Transform](https://protopia.ai/stained-glass-transform/) (a custom prompt-privacy encoder).

Example assistant message:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "reasoning": {
    "type": "prompt_embeds",
    "data": "<base64_encoded_tensor>"
  },
  "content": ""
}
```

The implementation changes two production files and delegates to the existing content-part parser. Reasoning embeddings are parsed before content embeddings to match their order in the rendered prompt. The existing `--enable-prompt-embeds` flag and tensor requirements apply, and the chat template must render `reasoning` or `reasoning_content`.

Open PR searches found no existing implementation of reasoning prompt embedding inputs. Related [PR #59930](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59930) addresses embedding decode budgets.

AI assistance was used in implementation, tests, documentation, and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM-5.3] Enable GLM low-latency BF16 GEMM on SM107
commits.pr_body:
## Overview


The GLM-5.2/5.3 low-latency BF16 GEMM selection (CuTe DSL skinny GEMM + `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` at decode batch sizes) is gated to SM103, so on VRNVL72 (SM107) every unquantized decode projection runs cuBLAS. This PR enables the selection on SM107 with a table swept on VRNVL72, the same way #54606 enabled the Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM plan on SM107.

## Claims


- **VRNVL72 coverage:** on SM107, GLM-5.2/5.3 BF16 decode projections use tuned CuTe DSL skinny GEMM / `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` configs where they beat cuBLAS. That covers fused qkv_a, q_b / indexer wq_b, o_proj (M ≤ 3), indexer wk + weights_proj, shared-expert gate_up / down and MTP eh_proj, at TP4. TP8 q_b keeps the existing SM103 row, re-measured on sm107.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization][Quark] Support MXFP8 (W8A8) routed experts
commits.pr_body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Support AMD Quark checkpoints whose routed experts are OCP MX MXFP8 (W8A8) instead of MXFP4/MXFP6, by adding a `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod`.

This also makes per-layer mixed checkpoints (some MoE layers MXFP8, others MXFP4) loadable, since Quark already resolves the scheme per layer.

## Claims

- A Quark checkpoint with MXFP8 (W8A8) routed experts now loads and serves instead of failing at model construction with `ValueError: Unsupported OCP MX dtype combination for MoE: input_dtype=mxfp8_e4m3, weight_dtype=mxfp8_e4m3`.
- MXFP8 experts use the existing MXFP8 MoE stack (`select_mxfp8_moe_backend`, `convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format`, `make_fp8_moe_kernel`), i.e. `AITER_MXFP8` on gfx950, with dynamic MXFP8 activations — no new kernel, no new weight layout.
- Per-layer mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 routed experts work with no change to Quark's config resolution: `layer_quant_config` entries matching `<layer>.experts*` select MXFP8 for that layer, everything else falls back to `global_quant_config`.
- Unsupported spellings fail early with an actionable error: only the 1-D `per_group`/`group_size=32`/`e8m0` weight spelling is accepted for MXFP8 experts (the 2-D `per_block` spelling is Linear-only), and biases are rejected.
- No change for existing MXFP4/MXFP6/INT8/FP8/NVFP4 Quark checkpoints.

## Validation

New and affected tests in `tests/quantization/test_quark.py`, on MI350:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  "tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_target[ocp_mx_mxfp8_activation]" \
  "tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_target[ocp_mx_mxfp8_per_block_experts]" \
  "tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_instantiation[ocp_mx_mxfp8_activation]" \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quant_method_dispatch_mixed_mxfp4_mxfp8_experts \
  tests/quantization/test_quark.py::test_quark_w8a8_mxfp8_moe_weight_shapes
```

```
5 passed, 14 warnings in 8.78s
```

The dispatch matrix these extend, which re-checks every pre-existing Quark scheme:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -k "dispatch_target or dispatch_instantiation" tests/quantization/test_quark.py
```

```
60 passed, 75 deselected, 14 warnings in 36.07s
```

- The `[ocp_mx_mxfp8_activation]` cases resolve W8A8 MXFP8 experts to `(kMxfp8Static, kMxfp8Dynamic, QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod)` and instantiate that method; `[ocp_mx_mxfp8_per_block_experts]` rejects the 2-D `per_block` spelling on experts.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mixed_mxfp4_mxfp8_experts` checks that a `<layer>.experts*` entry selects MXFP8 for that layer only, with other layers on the global MXFP4 and `shared_experts` unaffected.
- `test_quark_w8a8_mxfp8_moe_weight_shapes` checks the `[E, rows, cols]` E4M3 / `[E, rows, cols / 32]` uint8 parameter layout and the rejection of shapes not divisible by 32.

End-to-end accuracy of a Quark MXFP8 MoE checkpoint was not measured here; the numerics are those of the shared MXFP8 MoE path.

## Details

Quark resolves MoE schemes per layer (`global_quant_config` plus `layer_quant_config` globs), but `quark_moe.py` had no MXFP8 MoE method: `fp8_e4m3`/`per_group`/`group_size=32`/`e8m0` routed experts were dispatched to `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod`, which only implements MXFP4/MXFP6, and failed at model construction.

`QuarkW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod` mirrors `CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w8a8_mxfp8.py#L35).

Behavior changes:
- `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod` no longer declares MXFP8 in its `supported_*_quant_keys`, so MXFP8 experts are rejected by the shared `QuarkMoEMethod` validation instead of the later `OCP_MX_Scheme` check (its `ValueError` keeps upstream's wording),
- Quark checkpoints that previously failed to load now serve

Limitations:
- `hidden_size`/`intermediate_size_per_partition` must be divisible by 32,
- no bias,
- dynamic MXFP8 activations only, and the kernel comes from `select_mxfp8_moe_backend` (`AITER_MXFP8` on gfx950)

No new flag, config field or env var, so no docs change.

No duplicate work: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "quark mxfp8"` and `--search "mxfp8 MoE quark in:body"` return no PR adding a Quark MXFP8 MoE method; #61457 (per-layer fused shared expert) and #56523 (MXFP4 oracle) are distinct.

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] benchmark_moe: read Gemma 4's MoE shape from its text config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` crashes before tuning starts, so fused-MoE tile tables cannot be generated for Gemma 4. Same fix as #45789, which the stale bot closed for inactivity without review.

## Claims

- `benchmark_moe.py` tunes and benchmarks Gemma 4 MoE models (`Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`, `Gemma4ForCausalLM`) instead of raising `AttributeError: 'Gemma4TextConfig' object has no attribute 'num_local_experts'`.
- The tables it writes have the shape vLLM loads at runtime (`E=128,N=704` for 26B-A4B).
- A config with no MoE experts (dense Gemma 4 31B/E2B, or any dense model) now stops with `ValueError: <architecture> has no MoE experts in its config; benchmark_moe.py only tunes MoE layers.` instead of a `TypeError` in `ensure_divisibility` or an `AttributeError` on `num_local_experts` (raised in review by @chrikrah).

## Validation

On 1x H200 NVL; the first two rows on `main@852989f`, the tuning run on `main@2534a96`:

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it --tp-size 1 --dtype auto --batch-size 1 16 256` | `AttributeError ... num_local_experts` | runs; kernel time 43.9 / 265.5 / 437.0 us at batch 1 / 16 / 256 |
| same with `--dtype fp8_w8a8` | same error | runs; kernel time 31.5 / 152.2 / 258.0 us |
| `--tune` (fp8_w8a8, 11 batch sizes) | same error | writes `E=128,N=704,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json`; the server logs `Using configuration from ...` for it |

`get_model_params` on real configs (CPU, `transformers` `AutoConfig`), after the dense-config check:

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B | `(128, 8, 704, 2816)` |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, OLMoE-1B-7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Granite 3.1 3B-A800M | unchanged |
| Gemma 4 31B, Gemma 4 E2B, Qwen3-0.6B, SmolLM2-135M (dense) | `ValueError: ... has no MoE experts in its config` |

## Details

Gemma 4 architectures fell through to the Mixtral branch of `get_model_params()`. Gemma 4 keeps its MoE fields on the text config under the same names as DiffusionGemma (`num_experts`, `top_k_experts`, `moe_intermediate_size`), so it joins that branch. `moe_intermediate_size` (704) is the expert width; `intermediate_size` (2112) is the dense MLP's and would produce a table vLLM never loads.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][RL] Fix cross-stream reuse of packed NCCL receive buffers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62554. `packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer` lets the caching allocator hand a receive buffer to the next receive while a layerwise-reload replay on another slot stream still reads it. This corrupts MoE weights after packed NCCL weight updates.

## Claims

- Fixes silent weight corruption with packed NCCL weight transfer plus layerwise reload when a layer spans several packs (reproducer: 10/10 corrupted reloads on `main`, 0/10 with this PR).
- Orders every `post_unpack_func` after all earlier receives, instead of relying on NCCL's in-order completion.
- No measurable change in sync time; two-stream overlap is preserved.
- Same or lower peak memory than `main`, except layerwise reload over a slow transport, which reserves one to a few packs more because buffers with pending reads can no longer be reused early.

## Validation

All on this PR's head, 4x H100, torch 2.14.

- **New tests** (`pytest tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py -k DeferredConsumer`): 4 fail on `main` (20/20 runs), 4 pass here. The allocator test asserts the reuse directly via `data_ptr`s, so it fails on `main` regardless of GPU timing.
- **Upstream suites** (`test_packed_tensor.py`, `test_weight_transfer.py`, `test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py`, `test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py`, `test_reload.py`): 250 passed, 36 skipped, 2 xpassed, 0 failed.
- **Reproducer** (in the issue; real NCCL over NET, real `RoutedExperts`, real layerwise reload): 10/10 corrupted on `main`, 0/10 here.
- **Served** (`rlhf_http_nccl.py` layout, TP=2 OLMoE, NET): `/weight_checker` matched after every sync with per-expert, grouped per-expert and fused senders; greedy outputs identical to `main`.

**Latency** (`examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py`, median of 10–12 syncs):

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| opt-125m (example as written) | 61.9 ms | 61.7 ms |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 32 MB packs | 122.5 ms | 123.0 ms |
| OLMoE-1B-7B, 104 packs, NET | 4,886 ms | 4,929 ms |
| OLMoE-1B-7B, 13 packs (1 GB default), NET | 4,945 ms | 4,928 ms |

Overlap with 2 buffers is unchanged (NVLink 10.7 vs 10.8 ms; NET ~105 ms vs 189 ms serial, all builds within ±1.5%).

**Memory** (consumer peak reserved over baseline; `max_memory_allocated` doesn't count blocks held back by `record_stream`):

| scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate load, k buffers | 2k packs | k packs |
| Served OLMoE, NET, 1 GB packs, first sync / later syncs | 4,554 / +0 MB | 4,276 / +0 MB |
| Served OLMoE, NET, per-expert, 128 MB packs | 2,270 MB | 2,404 MB |
| Reproducer (layerwise), NET, 106 MB packs, 2 / 3 buffers | 2,400 / 3,276 MB | 2,764 / 3,384 MB |

Over NVLink the layerwise numbers match `main`.

## Details

- **`record_stream`** on each receive buffer, for every slot stream and the caller's stream, fixes the corruption: the allocator won't reissue a freed block until those streams pass the free. It also covers the buffer's own pending broadcast, so the consumer no longer keeps the previous pack of each slot alive.
- **Event chain** (one event per pack): each pack's callback waits on the previous pack's receive, so callbacks are ordered after all earlier receives. Receives are never delayed, and no callback waits on another callback.
- Each half alone passes only its own test.
- Larger `num_buffers` doesn't avoid the bug: with k buffers, a layer spanning at least k + 2 packs is exposed. The allocator test covers `num_buffers=3`.
- **Alternatives considered:** copying out in the callback (an extra copy of every weight); a host sync per replay (serializes the streams).
- `test_unpack_produces_independent_copies` is replaced by `test_unpack_returns_views`; the old test passed only because the packed buffer aliased the reference tensor.

Developed with AI assistance (Cursor); the submitter reviewed every line and ran the tests above.
